title: Janus Henderson Launches Tokenized Nasdaq-100 Fund JQQQ on Stellar
summary: Janus Henderson and Centrifuge have launched JQQQ, an issuer-sponsored blockchain-native fund seeking exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index through the Stellar network.
content:
TL;DR: Janus Henderson and Centrifuge have launched JQQQ, an issuer-sponsored blockchain-native fund seeking exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index through the Stellar network. The official source also identifies specific limits or future steps, so implementation and market impact should not be assumed.

Janus Henderson and Centrifuge have launched JQQQ, an issuer-sponsored blockchain-native fund seeking exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index through the Stellar network. For digital-asset markets, the important issue is less the announcement in isolation than the channel through which it could affect users, capital or network activity. The latest development deserves attention, but its relevance depends on the facts published by the organisation behind it and the work still required to make it matter.

What the primary announcement establishes

The October 27 announcement says Janus Henderson manages the strategy and Centrifuge provides the infrastructure for public-blockchain issuance and fund operations. The Nasdaq-100 index is licensed from Nasdaq, making this a fund strategy sponsored by its issuer rather than an unrelated synthetic token claiming a stock-market link.

JQQQ is structured as a British Virgin Islands segregated portfolio with Anemoy Asset Management as investment manager and Janus Henderson Investors US as sub-investment manager. The issuer says JQQQ is available only to eligible investors where lawful and is not available to US persons; the holdings do not grant shareholders direct rights in the underlying Nasdaq-100 securities.

Why this could matter for crypto markets

Offering familiar benchmark exposure through a digital share register tests whether asset managers can use blockchain systems to serve qualified investors while preserving portfolio management, transfer rules and disclosures. The public-chain element may allow new distribution and collateral arrangements, but those possibilities depend on third parties and law. It is important to distinguish exposure to an index from ownership of the index constituents.

For financial institutions, a technical link is only the beginning. They must also settle liability, account for funds, control access and recover from a failed transfer. That is why announced partnerships are best judged by operating detail rather than by the number of logos appearing in a release. That distinction matters to investors trying to separate a plausible structural change from a headline that may not immediately move price or onchain activity.

The limits of the headline

Tokenization does not remove investment risk, and future lending or collateral uses are not services automatically provided by Janus Henderson. The fund can deviate from the reference index and may not trade as freely as an exchange-listed ETF.

Consider the difference between holding a token and using it in an everyday business process. Treasury teams and trading desks need reconciliation, internal approvals, liquidity at the point of conversion and an auditable record. Projects that solve those edges may have more practical impact than projects that simply shorten onchain confirmation times.

The wider context

Janus Henderson and Centrifuge launch JQQQ sits within a wider shift toward tokenized index funds. This area has a recurring challenge: the benefits are easiest to describe before the operational details are complete. Different stakeholders measure success differently. A user wants clarity and predictable access; an operator wants reliable controls and manageable costs; an institution wants accountability if something fails. Those perspectives can be in tension, and the source announcement should be read with that in mind.

The distinction also shapes how to read future updates. A new partnership, proposal or software version is a verifiable milestone. Adoption, consistent performance and financial effects require additional evidence. That is why follow-up reporting should distinguish released features, planned features and measured use rather than combining them into one claim.

What to watch next

Look for actual subscriptions, approved distribution channels, custody arrangements and whether onchain investors can redeem reliably through market stress.

Adoption is rarely a single launch moment. It typically moves from a commercial agreement to limited implementation, onboarding, real transaction volume and eventually routine usage. Keeping those stages separate matters when evaluating institutional blockchain announcements. The next evidence should come from official implementation updates and measurable outcomes, not from assuming that a news release guarantees adoption or a token-price response.

Primary source: Janus Henderson and Centrifuge launch JQQQ (published 2026-10-27).

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Ripple CEO Praises US Treasury Secretary as Major Crypto Deals Unfold
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse credited Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent with supporting responsible U.S. crypto growth as Swell began. His remarks extended a history of endorsements as the conference featured new corporate treasury capabilities and financial partnerships. Garlinghouse Praises Bessent...
content:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse credited Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent with supporting responsible U.S. crypto growth as Swell began. His remarks extended a history of endorsements as the conference featured new corporate treasury capabilities and financial partnerships.

Key Takeaways

  • Bessent joined Garlinghouse to open Swell’s 10th edition.
  • Garlinghouse previously backed Bessent’s selection and legislative push.
  • Ripple introduced returns targeting corporate cash outside banking hours.

Garlinghouse Praises Bessent’s Crypto Leadership

Brad Garlinghouse, CEO of blockchain infrastructure company Ripple, praised Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the current administration on Oct. 27. In his comments on Bessent’s crypto leadership on X, Garlinghouse thanked the secretary for opening Swell with him as the company disclosed partnerships and highlighted its federal banking approval.

Garlinghouse described Bessent’s participation as an honor, crediting his leadership with helping the domestic crypto industry develop. He stated:

“His leadership, alongside the current administration, has been instrumental in ensuring that responsible crypto can thrive in the US. I’m extremely grateful he spent time with us today.”

Swell’s expanded conference program runs Oct. 27-29 at The Shed in Manhattan, bringing together financial executives, developers, and researchers. The event combines Swell, Apex, and UBRI Connect, with more than 100 speakers and over 80 sessions spanning digital asset markets, payments, institutional finance, and technology.

Bessent Endorsement Began Before His Treasury Tenure

The executive’s endorsement of Bessent’s Treasury selection dates to November 2024, when President-elect Donald Trump chose him for the position. Garlinghouse called Bessent “the perfect pick” and predicted that he would support crypto and innovation. His latest comments assessed the secretary’s leadership after he took office.

Policy alignment continued in September through Garlinghouse’s support for Bessent’s CLARITY Act push. On Sept. 14, Garlinghouse urged senators to support the negotiated legislation, arguing that policymakers had made substantial compromises. Bessent’s case included proposed Treasury authority to respond if stablecoin-related deposit flight harmed community banks.

Corporate Cash Offering Targets Nights and Weekends

Alongside his praise of Bessent, Garlinghouse highlighted Ripple Treasury’s 24/7 Returns feature in the same Swell update. Introduced Oct. 26, the offering is designed to help eligible corporate customers generate returns on qualifying digital assets, targeting operating cash that would otherwise remain idle overnight, over weekends, and during holidays. Qualifying assets must be held in a Ripple wallet, with participation subject to program requirements.

Ripple USD (RLUSD), the company’s dollar-backed stablecoin, counts among the qualifying assets eligible for returns. Businesses can participate without independently managing the underlying digital asset transactions. Alongside the returns feature, artificial intelligence tools coordinate cash positioning, forecasting, reconciliation, liquidity management, and payments within the platform.

Commercial developments included Robinhood’s agreement with Ripple, covering customer-facing services, institutional financing, and treasury operations. Garlinghouse also highlighted expanded BNY cooperation across custody and proposed tokenized trade finance, plus final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank. He indicated that further announcements would follow during the conference week.

title: Fed’s hawkish rate hold keeps pressure on Bitcoin: Analysts
summary: Traders are pricing in a 78% chance of a December rate hike, while analysts say Treasury yields, the US dollar and upcoming inflation data could determine Bitcoin’s next move.
content:
Bitcoin could face further headwinds after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady while signaling continued concern about inflation, according to market analysts. 

The Fed voted 10-2 Wednesday to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4%, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favoring a quarter-point increase. 

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged that inflation remained above the central bank’s 2% target. 

“Americans… are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the Committee’s objective for close to 6 years. It’s our responsibility to get inflation down,” he said.

Iggy Ioppe, chief investment officer at tokenization platform Theo, said the decision itself was widely expected, but investors had not fully anticipated the Fed’s hawkish messaging. 

“Markets had the hold priced, but not the hawkish tone,” he said in comments sent to Cointelegraph.

There are expectations that the Fed will raise rates in its Dec. 8-9 meeting, and again next year.

CME FedWatch data showed traders assigning a 78.4% probability to a quarter-point increase by December and a 67.3% probability of at least a quarter-point increase by March, as of Wednesday. 

Warsh declined to say whether the Fed would raise rates at the end of the year. 

“A lot of things can happen, so I’m not going to be able to share with you my musings about what happens when this group gets together six weeks from now,” he said during a press conference.

At elevated interest rates, Bitcoin has to “compete with” a risk-free rate near 4%, said Ioppe.

Related: Bitcoin price bounce rejected at 50-day trend line ahead of FOMC, earnings

However, Bitget analyst Lewis Huang said Bitcoin’s next move could depend less on the Fed’s decision itself than on Treasury yields, the US dollar and broader investor sentiment. 

“With limited new direction from the Fed, Bitcoin’s near-term performance may depend more heavily on Treasury yields, dollar movements and broader risk sentiment,” he said. 

Analysts, including Huang, are now looking to Thursday’s personal consumption expenditures inflation report and earnings from major technology companies for clues about the direction of risk assets. 

Sygnum Bank chief investment officer Fabian Dori agreed, adding that “the next couple of days promise more excitement” with Thursday’s release of PCE inflation data.

“Various Mag 7 companies reporting earnings this week will help clarify whether AI capex is turning into revenues. Following these short-term catalysts, broader liquidity and financial conditions are likely to shape the path towards the December decision,” he added. 

Magazine: Crypto could outperform AI stocks: Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser

title: SEC Crypto Custody Proposal Could Expand Options for Advisers and Funds
summary: The SEC has proposed a tailored custody framework for investment advisers and registered funds that handle crypto assets.
content:
TL;DR: The SEC has proposed a tailored custody framework for investment advisers and registered funds that handle crypto assets. The official source also identifies specific limits or future steps, so implementation and market impact should not be assumed.

The SEC has proposed a tailored custody framework for investment advisers and registered funds that handle crypto assets. For digital-asset markets, the important issue is less the announcement in isolation than the channel through which it could affect users, capital or network activity. The latest development deserves attention, but its relevance depends on the facts published by the organisation behind it and the work still required to make it matter.

What the primary announcement establishes

The proposal was published October 1 under the Investment Advisers Act and Investment Company Act frameworks. It would address the custody of crypto assets while modifying requirements involving adviser audits and broker-dealer custodial services.

The SEC says the proposed approach could permit self-custody in specified circumstances and use of state trust companies as custodians. The agency set a public comment period of 60 days after publication in the Federal Register; the changes have not been finalised.

Why this could matter for crypto markets

The difficult issue in institutional crypto is often not whether someone can hold a private key, but how an adviser proves control, segregation and responsibility to clients and regulators. A tailored framework may offer new options for legally supervised access, yet each option carries different custody, governance and cyber risks. Consultation is where those trade-offs need to be tested.

Regulation can change the economics of a product without changing a line of smart-contract code. Authorisation, reserve custody, supervisory reporting and customer eligibility can determine where a digital asset is available and which institutions may handle it. That distinction matters to investors trying to separate a plausible structural change from a headline that may not immediately move price or onchain activity.

The limits of the headline

This is a proposal, not a currently effective blanket permission for every registered fund or adviser to self-custody assets. The details and final scope may change after public feedback.

Regulated access is not the same as an investment recommendation. Even a service supervised by a public agency can face market risk, operational failures, changing prices or limitations on the protections available to holders.

The wider context

SEC proposed crypto custody framework sits within a wider shift toward fund custody. This area has a recurring challenge: the benefits are easiest to describe before the operational details are complete. Different stakeholders measure success differently. A user wants clarity and predictable access; an operator wants reliable controls and manageable costs; an institution wants accountability if something fails. Those perspectives can be in tension, and the source announcement should be read with that in mind.

The distinction also shapes how to read future updates. A new partnership, proposal or software version is a verifiable milestone. Adoption, consistent performance and financial effects require additional evidence. That is why follow-up reporting should distinguish released features, planned features and measured use rather than combining them into one claim.

What to watch next

Watch for comment submissions, revisions, the final rulemaking timetable and how custodians adapt service models if the proposal progresses.

The important question for firms is how a rule translates into actual procedures. Written compliance policies, customer disclosure, testing and ongoing reporting often prove more consequential than the headline date of an announcement. The next evidence should come from official implementation updates and measurable outcomes, not from assuming that a news release guarantees adoption or a token-price response.

Primary source: SEC proposed crypto custody framework (published 2026-10-01).

title: Ripple Roars Toward $900M Milestone as XRP Gains Wall Street Access
summary: Ripple is approaching a projected $900 million annualized product revenue run rate as institutional custody and payment channels expand around XRP. Its growth strategy combines payments, trading, treasury management, and digital asset infrastructure. Ripple Targets $900M as XRP Access Expands Ripple...
content:
Ripple is approaching a projected $900 million annualized product revenue run rate as institutional custody and payment channels expand around XRP. Its growth strategy combines payments, trading, treasury management, and digital asset infrastructure.

Key Takeaways

  • Institutional XRP custody expands through BNY’s digital asset platform.
  • Ripple expects to reach its projected revenue run rate by year-end.
  • XRP payment support and proposed trade finance initiatives broaden access.

Ripple Targets $900M as XRP Access Expands

Ripple said Oct. 28 that it was on track to reach a $900 million annualized product revenue run rate by year-end, reflecting product growth and integration of businesses acquired in 2025. That means revenue at the projected year-end pace would total $900 million over 12 months.

The company is bringing those businesses together so customers can combine payments, custody, stablecoins, prime brokerage, and treasury management. Customers and partners using multiple solutions had tripled this year, Ripple said, naming BNY, brokerage infrastructure provider DriveWealth, Robinhood, and Water.org, a nonprofit expanding access to safe water and sanitation.

Brad Garlinghouse, CEO of Ripple, stated:

“Ripple is at the epicenter of this massive transformation to rewire the world’s financial system, solving the inefficiencies that have slowed money movement for decades with digital assets like XRP.”

Institutional XRP Access Extends From Custody to Payments

BNY’s expanded relationship with Ripple brings XRP into an established bank custody service. Eligible institutional clients can now safeguard, hold, and transfer XRP and Ripple USD (RLUSD) through BNY’s Digital Asset Custody platform, the bank confirmed Oct. 27. The Bank of New York Mellon Corp. (NYSE: BNY) provides that access within its existing governance and operational controls.

The collaboration also extends to proposed uses for the XRP Ledger, including tokenized trade finance with C2FO, a working capital platform. The companies are exploring supply chain finance, which helps suppliers receive early payment for approved invoices, with the aim of broadening investor access. Implementation depends on client requirements.

Alongside that initiative, the bank intends to support more tokenized assets and investment products issued on the ledger. Those plans, together with direct RLUSD minting and redemption, remain subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals. Both plans are meant to make payments, settlement, and collateral workflows more efficient over time.

Payment access is expanding through wallet infrastructure as well. Privy, a Stripe company, is supporting payments with XRP, RLUSD, and other digital assets on the XRP Ledger through programmable wallets, Ripple said. Businesses and developers can use that infrastructure to incorporate digital asset payments into applications, including those built for AI agents.

Robinhood Partnership Connects Trading With Treasury Operations

Ripple’s strategy of combining services also underpins its agreement with Robinhood Markets Inc. (Nasdaq: HOOD), which spans stablecoin settlement, treasury management, and institutional trading. Robinhood plans to use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for institutional settlement and integrate Ripple Treasury into its own financial operations.

Supporting those stablecoin services is a broader regulatory structure, strengthened by Ripple’s Oct. 26 disclosure of final national trust bank approval. The federally chartered institution is approved to manage segregated RLUSD reserves and act as collateral trustee for holders’ benefit, and it will be authorized to offer fiduciary digital asset custody once it opens. Segregation keeps those assets separate from the issuer’s other holdings.

Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple’s New York-regulated trust company, will continue issuing RLUSD, a dollar-backed stablecoin designed to maintain a value of $1 per token. Ripple reported that RLUSD had reached a $2.6 billion market capitalization as its uses expanded across the company’s financial services.

title: The Betting Probe Behind Flávio Bolsonaro’s Escape From Brazil
summary: Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the U.S. after ignoring a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. The order was issued in a money-laundering probe into his ties with a lawyer, who the government’s betting regulator found to be the country’s ...
content:
Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the U.S. after ignoring a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. The order was issued in a money-laundering probe into his ties with a lawyer, who the government’s betting regulator found to be the country’s largest depositor on betting sites in 2025.

Key Takeaways

  • Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil after ignoring an order to surrender his passports in a betting laundering probe.
  • Brazil’s betting regulator says his ally Willer Tomaz deposited over $48.2 million on betting sites in 2025.

The Passport Order Was Issued in a Betting Case

Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s Oct. 25 presidential runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, crossed into Argentina on Tuesday night with his wife and two daughters and boarded a private jet to Guayaquil, Ecuador, about 40 minutes later, according to Argentina’s migration authority. The plane landed in Miami on Wednesday morning, according to flight-tracking data cited by Brazilian media. The U.S. government said it would issue visas to the senator and his family, and President Donald Trump said he would approve their entry.

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered Bolsonaro on Oct. 26 to hand over his Brazilian and Italian passports within 24 hours, barred him from leaving Brazil, and banned him from contacting lawyer Willer Tomaz. The Federal Police had cited a “concrete and current” risk of flight, pointing to the senator’s economic power, structures abroad that could support a long stay, and his brother Eduardo’s public suggestion that he leave Brazil if he lost the election. When the deadline passed, the police canceled his passports.

Bolsonaro is suspected, alongside Tomaz, “of money laundering through betting platforms,” state news agency Agência Brasil reported. On the day the order was served, Bolsonaro called it persecution and insisted he would stay.

“I never thought of leaving the country,” he said. “I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this aberration, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me, but no one will silence me.”

The investigation, which began as a Federal Police probe in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, looks at suspected money laundering and currency evasion. Investigators suspect Bolsonaro and Tomaz are hidden partners in Best Bet—a betting site Tomaz founded and controlled, according to Exame—and in Alcazar Holdings, a company based in Madeira, Portugal, where Bolsonaro allegedly appears as a “master” user on a bank account. They flagged about $24.3 million (R$130 million) in suspicious transactions between March and May 2025, an amount described as incompatible with the senator’s known activities.

The two men deny any business partnership, and Tomaz’s defense denies that Bolsonaro had access to the account. On Oct. 23, Moraes ordered a freeze of up to $1.1 billion (R$6 billion) of Tomaz’s assets, a ceiling rather than an amount actually found. Tomaz left Brazil in August and lives in the U.S.

Tomaz is no ordinary gambler. A technical note from the Finance Ministry’s Secretariat of Prizes and Bets (SPA), dated Oct. 1 and revealed by UOL, found that he deposited more than $48.2 million (R$258 million) on betting sites in 2025—nearly double the next-largest depositor, and withdrew about $37.4 million (R$200 million). The note puts his total betting volume at around $935 million (R$5 billion), a turnover figure that counts winnings bet again. Tomaz’s representatives say his funds are lawful and declared to tax authorities, and that the betting volume “does not represent new money.”

The regulator said betting brand Blaze failed to flag his transactions, including 14 deposits of about $93,500 (R$500,000) each in a single day in October 2025, followed the next day by 12 withdrawals of the same size in 18 minutes. It also said there appeared to be “signs of negligence or intent” by the operator.

A separate inquiry into possible foreign support for Bolsonaro’s campaign has a prediction market angle. Justice Flávio Dino on Oct. 27 ordered the Federal Police to identify, among other things, who paid for ads by foreign accounts that promoted Polymarket odds favoring the senator. Polymarket, which is barred in Brazil, had priced Bolsonaro as the favorite before Lula’s comeback. Dino’s order does not conclude that any crime occurred, and the campaign denies receiving foreign financing.

Bolsonaro leaves behind a sector in limbo. The country’s 85 betting licenses lapsed on the day of the runoff under a provisional measure banning sports betting and online casinos, and Lula has said betting would not come back. The Supreme Court has scheduled a Nov. 3 public hearing on challenges to the ban.

title: Swiss FINMA Approves First Domestic Retail Bitcoin ETF
summary: Switzerland’s FINMA has approved its first Swiss-law retail exchange-traded fund that invests directly in Bitcoin.

The regulator announced the approval on October 20 and classified the fund as an alternative-investment product carrying specific risk. FINMA says Bitcoin’s trading history and liquidity supported an exemption from ordinary diversification requirements.

title: $250M FalconX Facility Powers Ibis Push Into Onchain Credit
summary: Onchain credit platform Ibis has launched out of stealth, securing a $250 million credit facility from FalconX alongside a closed pre-seed round. Funding and Strategic Backing Onchain credit platform Ibis announced its emergence from stealth on Oct. 28, backed by a $250 million credit facility from ...
content:
Onchain credit platform Ibis has launched out of stealth, securing a $250 million credit facility from FalconX alongside a closed pre-seed round.

Key Takeaways

  • Ibis exited stealth with a $250M credit facility from FalconX and pre-seed capital from top crypto firms.
  • Anchorage Digital Bank will custody assets, helping bring regulated credit infrastructure to digital assets.
  • Ibis plans to expand its onchain financing model into GPU infrastructure, robotics, and venture capital.

Funding and Strategic Backing

Onchain credit platform Ibis announced its emergence from stealth on Oct. 28, backed by a $250 million credit facility from digital asset financial services firm FalconX and the completion of its pre-seed funding round.

The pre-seed round was led by FalconX alongside a syndicate of digital asset and capital markets institutional investors, including Anchorage Digital, Innovating Capital, and executives from Revolut, Injective Foundation, Superstate, Agora, Blockchain.com, and Pyth, among others.

Over the past few years, FalconX has focused on bridging institutional capital and onchain debt markets through structured credit products and tokenized lending. In August, it partnered with Ethena Labs on a $1 billion warehouse financing facility via a special purpose vehicle (SPV). The facility deploys capital backed by USDe into overcollateralized institutional credit loans serviced and managed by FalconX.

It has expanded its tokenized credit products and onchain lending vaults onto emerging Layer 1 and Layer 2 networks, incorporating automated margin controls, real-time collateral monitoring, and onchain settlement.

Ibis, meanwhile, operates an end-to-end institutional credit platform designed to originate, tokenize, underwrite, risk-manage, and service structured credit facilities. The company aims to address a long-standing structural gap in frontier markets, where traditional lending infrastructure frequently fails to support emerging industries with non-standard collateral and complex risk profiles.

“Frontier markets are developing faster than the financial infrastructure built to support them,” said Cooper Emmons, founder and CEO of Ibis. “Today, many high-quality businesses with strong fundamentals are underserved, not because they lack creditworthiness, but because traditional underwriters refuse to innovate.”

The platform initially targets institutions in the digital asset and prediction markets sectors, with plans to expand its credit infrastructure to additional frontier market segments.

Under the operational model, Anchorage Digital Bank will serve as a custody, banking, and design partner to ensure collateral is secured in a regulated environment. Venture capital firm Innovating Capital will provide expertise in transaction structuring, risk management, and strategic development.

“Access to reliable, institutional-grade credit is an important part of the continued maturation of digital assets,” said Joshua Lim, co-head of global markets at FalconX. “Ibis is building infrastructure to help bridge the gap between institutional capital allocators and a new generation of onchain market participants.”

Institutional Industry Support

Institutional backing for the platform highlights growing demand for disciplined, yield-bearing structured credit products designed specifically for digital asset trading firms and emerging Web3 businesses.

“Credit is one of the last pieces of institutional infrastructure that digital asset markets are still building,” said Nathan McCauley, CEO and co-founder of Anchorage Digital. “Ibis is taking a disciplined approach: structured facilities, real underwriting, and collateral held in regulated custody at Anchorage Digital Bank. That combination is what lets institutional capital participate with confidence.”

Ibis’ investor roster includes high-profile industry executives, such as Jordi Alexander (CEO, Selini), Shiliang Tang (managing partner, Monarq Asset Management), Mirza Uddin (COO, Injective Foundation), Roshun Patel (head of credit and alternatives, Erebor), and Nick van Eck (CEO, Agora).

title: Ethereum Researchers Explore Transaction Assertions to Reduce Signing Risks
summary: Ethereum Foundation researchers are examining native transaction assertions that could make transaction safety depend on the final state as well as the signed instructions.
content:
TL;DR: Ethereum Foundation researchers are examining native transaction assertions that could make transaction safety depend on the final state as well as the signed instructions. The official source also identifies specific limits or future steps, so implementation and market impact should not be assumed.

Ethereum Foundation researchers are examining native transaction assertions that could make transaction safety depend on the final state as well as the signed instructions. For digital-asset markets, the important issue is less the announcement in isolation than the channel through which it could affect users, capital or network activity. The latest development deserves attention, but its relevance depends on the facts published by the organisation behind it and the work still required to make it matter.

What the primary announcement establishes

The foundation describes blind signing and uncertain execution outcomes as distinct ways users can approve actions with unwanted results. The research explores checks that inspect net balance, storage or code changes after execution and revert the transaction if a required rule fails.

EIP-7906 is a possible route, using a read-only post-transaction frame to evaluate changes and events before accepting the outcome. The foundation states that EIP-7906 is under consideration, not yet confirmed for a future upgrade, and would still require wallets or protocols to enforce a rule.

Why this could matter for crypto markets

A transaction signature proves authorisation of certain bytes; it does not by itself guarantee that a complex smart-contract interaction achieves the signer’s economic objective. Independent checks over final balances or approvals could narrow that gap. Yet they introduce design choices about who defines the rule, how much gas it costs and whether third-party software can silently omit it.

Blockchain infrastructure does not improve in a vacuum. Engineers must consider existing applications, node operators, client compatibility and how errors behave under stressed conditions. A change that appears straightforward at the protocol level can create a demanding coordination problem. That distinction matters to investors trying to separate a plausible structural change from a headline that may not immediately move price or onchain activity.

The limits of the headline

This is research and proposal-level work, not a new safety guarantee available for ordinary Ethereum transactions today. Assertions sourced from a compromised interface could still encode a harmful outcome.

Performance claims also require careful definitions. Throughput, finality, responsiveness, cost and fault tolerance are different measurements. Improving one does not automatically improve all of them, especially when a wallet, exchange or application adds its own confirmations.

The wider context

Ethereum native transaction assertions sits within a wider shift toward wallet security. This area has a recurring challenge: the benefits are easiest to describe before the operational details are complete. Different stakeholders measure success differently. A user wants clarity and predictable access; an operator wants reliable controls and manageable costs; an institution wants accountability if something fails. Those perspectives can be in tension, and the source announcement should be read with that in mind.

The distinction also shapes how to read future updates. A new partnership, proposal or software version is a verifiable milestone. Adoption, consistent performance and financial effects require additional evidence. That is why follow-up reporting should distinguish released features, planned features and measured use rather than combining them into one claim.

What to watch next

Watch for EIP governance, wallet implementations, protocol support and testing of the proposed state-difference opcodes.

The operational test comes after the proposal or release note: can different client teams implement it, can developers upgrade safely and can users rely on it when activity spikes? That is the difference between an attractive design and durable infrastructure. The next evidence should come from official implementation updates and measurable outcomes, not from assuming that a news release guarantees adoption or a token-price response.

Primary source: Ethereum native transaction assertions (published 2026-10-05).

title: Canadian ‘crypto king’ case to go to jury as criminal trial winds down
summary: Aiden Pleterski, facing fraud charges in Canada over his alleged role in a digital asset Ponzi scheme, said that he was innocent at closing.
content:
Aiden Pleterski, facing fraud charges in Canada over his alleged role in a digital asset Ponzi scheme, said that he was innocent at closing.

The criminal case of Aiden Pleterski, the self-described “crypto king” who was allegedly behind a Ponzi scheme involving digital assets, will go to jury deliberations after closing arguments this week. 

According to Wednesday reporting from CBC, the jury overseeing Pleterski’s case will begin deliberations on Thursday after receiving final instructions from Justice Shaun Nakatsuru. Pleterski allegedly defrauded his social media followers out of about $30 million between 2021 and 2022. He was charged with fraud in 2024 and had been awaiting trial for more than two years, choosing to represent himself in court.

“I am innocent of these charges,” said Pleterski, according to CBC. “That is why I pled not guilty. Had I not been forced to represent myself, that would have been proven. That’s all I have to say.”

The fraud charge against the “crypto king” could result in a prison sentence of up to 14 years should he be found guilty at trial. Pleterski is one of many high-profile figures tied to the crypto industry accused of fraud, though others have already been convicted. Former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year prison sentence in the United States following his 2023 fraud conviction.

In a separate criminal case, five men, some of whom were reportedly victims of Pleterski’s scheme, were charged with kidnapping and torturing the “crypto king” in 2022. One of the men, Deren Akyeam-Pong, pleaded guilty to nine charges and awaits sentencing.

title: CFTC Revives Polymarket Probe as VPN Insider Case Heads to Trial: Reuters
summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is again examining whether Polymarket broke its 2022 promise to keep Americans off its offshore platform, Reuters reported. The report landed a day after a federal judge refused to dismiss charges against a soldier accused of reaching that platform throu...
content:
The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is again examining whether Polymarket broke its 2022 promise to keep Americans off its offshore platform, Reuters reported. The report landed a day after a federal judge refused to dismiss charges against a soldier accused of reaching that platform through a VPN to bet on the Maduro raid.

Key Takeaways

  • The CFTC is probing whether Polymarket failed to keep U.S. users off its offshore platform, per Reuters.
  • The inquiry covers Polymarket’s location controls, U.S. advertising, and onboarding on its U.S. platform.
  • A judge refused to dismiss charges against a soldier accused of making $400,000 on insider bets via a VPN.

Geolocation Controls Back Under the Microscope

The CFTC is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban U.S. users from its main overseas platform, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing two people familiar with the matter. The inquiry revives one the agency closed last year without bringing charges, and sits inside a broader investigation the CFTC opened into the company earlier this year.

According to the sources, the agency is examining how Polymarket determines where its customers are located and its advertising activities in the U.S. It is also scrutinizing the onboarding processes and customer protections on Polymarket’s U.S. platform. One of the people said the focus is on the company’s past controls and processes. Spokespeople for the CFTC and Polymarket declined to comment, and Reuters noted that probes are not necessarily an indication of wrongdoing.

The 2022 deal dates to January of that year, when the CFTC fined Polymarket $1.4 million for offering unregistered event-based binary options. As 2024 U.S. election betting on the platform grew, the CFTC opened a probe into whether Polymarket was complying with the settlement, the Justice Department opened a related investigation, and the FBI searched CEO Shayne Coplan’s New York home in November 2024.

Both agencies closed their probes in July 2025, and Polymarket bought a CFTC-licensed exchange and began relaunching in the U.S. late last year. Reuters said the new details “raise fresh questions” over why those earlier probes were closed. A Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment.

The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg first reported a broad CFTC probe of Polymarket in June, shortly after the Journal found that Polymarket paid creators to stage fake winnings in a campaign aimed at U.S. users, the platform was barred from serving.

The geolocation question is also central to what prosecutors call the first insider-trading prosecution of a prediction market trader. U.S. District Judge Margaret Garnett on Monday denied a motion to dismiss the indictment of Army Master Sergeant Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who is accused of betting on Polymarket ahead of the U.S. operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and turning about $34,000 into more than $400,000. According to the indictment, Van Dyke accessed Polymarket’s offshore platform using a VPN and an “exit mode” that geolocated to a foreign country.

Van Dyke pleaded not guilty in April, and his lawyers argued that his wagers were not illegal swaps under federal commodities law. Garnett ruled that question could not be settled at this stage, writing that the motion could succeed “only if the event contracts alleged in the indictment cannot be swaps as a matter of law, and Van Dyke has failed to make that showing.” His trial is tentatively scheduled for Dec. 7.

Polymarket has said it referred the Van Dyke matter to authorities and that it has revamped its controls. The platform said it expressly prohibits VPNs and similar tools used to get around its geographic restrictions. Its global head of investigations and intelligence, Shana Bautista, told Reuters in August that U.S. users circumventing the restrictions was not “a really prevalent issue.” This week, Bautista told NPR that Polymarket had investigated dozens of bets tied to the midterm elections ahead of the Nov. 3 vote.

title: Tokenized Stocks Hit $3.84B as Apple, Microsoft Move Onchain
summary: The tokenized-equity market has climbed to roughly $3.84 billion as major U.S. stocks increasingly move onto public blockchains. Base is putting companies including Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon onchain, turning earnings season into a real-time test for programmable equities. Coinbase Pushe...
content:
The tokenized-equity market has climbed to roughly $3.84 billion as major U.S. stocks increasingly move onto public blockchains. Base is putting companies including Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon onchain, turning earnings season into a real-time test for programmable equities.

Key Takeaways

  • Tokenized equities reached about $3.84B, with 4.5M holder addresses across public blockchains.
  • Base now hosts stocks like Apple and Microsoft, with Aave enabling some as USDC collateral.
  • The bigger opportunity is whether programmable stocks can sustain 24/7 trading, lending, and liquidity.

Coinbase Pushes Tokenized Stocks Deeper Into DeFi on Base

Wall Street’s earnings season is starting to play out on blockchain rails.

Tokenized versions of some of America’s largest companies, including Apple, Google parent Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Tesla, and Strategy, are now available on Base, the Coinbase-backed Ethereum Layer 2 network, where eligible investors outside the U.S. can hold and trade blockchain-based representations of the underlying shares.

The broader tokenized-stock market has reached approximately $3.84 billion in distributed value, up nearly 18% over the past 30 days, according to Blockworks data.

For crypto, that is becoming difficult to dismiss as an experiment.

Earnings Season Gets a 24/7 Market

Base has been highlighting tokenized Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Eli Lilly, and Strategy shares as the companies move through a major earnings week.

Unlike traditional brokerage accounts, tokenized equities can move through blockchain infrastructure around the clock and interact with DeFi applications.

Coinbase-issued stocks on Base are backed by real U.S. shares held with a regulated custodian, and use the B20 token standard. Base says they can be transferred, traded, and integrated into other applications, subject to eligibility restrictions.

“All asset classes are moving onchain,” Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong wrote on X. “Tokenized stocks and stablecoins are growing fast, with more to come.”

Stocks Are Becoming Programmable Collateral

Trading is only part of the opportunity.

Tokenized equities can increasingly be paired with other assets, supplied to liquidity markets or used as collateral. Aave, for example, now supports seven Coinbase tokenized U.S. stocks as collateral for USDC borrowing on Base.

Base is also offering ecosystem support to developers building products around programmable stocks, including credit markets and new brokerage experiences.

That changes the pitch from putting stocks on blockchain to making stocks usable inside crypto-native financial applications.

$3.84 Billion Signals a Market Taking Shape

The market remains tiny compared with the tens of trillions of dollars represented by conventional equities.

But its growth rate is becoming the headline.

Onchain data shows tokenized-stock value has climbed sharply in recent months, with bStocks, Ondo, xStocks, Securitize, and Coinbase among the major platforms competing for market share.

Blockworks co-founder Jason Yanowitz called tokenized equities one of technology’s fastest-growing charts. The next test is whether activity persists after the novelty fades.

If tokenized stocks develop deep liquidity, lending markets, and sustained 24/7 trading, then putting Apple or Nvidia onchain will no longer be the story. What investors can do with those shares after they arrive will be.

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Above $81,500 as Fed Keeps Rates Steady in Split Vote
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Above $81,500 as Fed Keeps Rates Steady in Split Vote
Bitcoin price held near $81,000 after the Federal Reserve kept rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote.
This post Bitcoin Price Trades Above $81,500 as Fed Keeps Rates Steady in Split Vote first appeared on Bitc...
content:
The Federal Reserve left its benchmark rate unchanged Wednesday, holding the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4%. The bitcoin price showed some volatility around $81,000.

The decision passed 10-2, and the dissents carry as much weight as the outcome. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point increase. It is the first time since 1992 that a Fed governor and a regional bank president have dissented together on the same side.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh faced reporters after the vote and said politics played no role in the decision, days before the midterm elections. Warsh has said he does not favor forward guidance absent a crisis, which leaves investors to read the data themselves. 

The committee’s statement dropped its earlier language about when a hike might support a return to 2% inflation. In its place is a line saying more information will guide the policy stance. The Fed also described growth as strong, up from solid.

The signal points toward tightening. Fed funds futures and the Fed’s own dot plot lean toward a rate increase by December, and some pricing puts the odds near three in four. Inflation has been running hot, and the two dissenters are the officials who want to act on it.

Bitcoin price reaction

Bitcoin price’s reaction was restrained. The bitcoin price spiked to about $81,700 in the minutes after the announcement, fell below $80,500, and then recovered toward $81,000. Most traders expected a hold, so the muted move surprises nobody.

Bitcoin’s first response to Fed news tends to be modest, and that the real direction often emerges over the following day. Spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $110 million in net inflows on October 26 and $176 million on October 27, a sign that some institutional money is buying the dip. Other observers have flagged large holders selling into strength.

That tension defines crypto’s position right now. Bitcoin sits about a third below its October 2025 record near $126,000. A rate-hike path works against an asset that has thrived on cheap money, and the market has spent months adjusting to the possibility that the easy-money era is over. 

Some traders read the hold as evidence the Fed will move slowly. Others see December as the real test. For now, the level to watch is a bitcoin price of $80,000. It has held as support in recent sessions, and a clean break below it would expose the next floor. 

Warsh and his colleagues have said they will wait for incoming data before acting. Bitcoin will have to wait along with everyone else.

Midterms up next

Bitcoin’s next big political test arrives on November 3, when voters across the country head to the polls. Crypto has not really dominated the campaign trail. 

The crypto industry spent about $176 million on more than 100 midterm races to build a bipartisan bloc in Congress that could protect its interests after President Donald Trump left office. Fairshake, the industry’s largest super PAC, led the effort and directed strategy as it had in the 2024 cycle.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is $81,478.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Strategy shareholders approved daily dividend payments across four preferred stocks, Coinbase said customer contact information was exposed through a third-party analytics provider and Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev warned that regulatory uncertainty could discourage investors from moving substantial assets into tokenized markets.

Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends across four preferred stocks

Strategy shareholders have approved a proposal to introduce daily dividend payments across the company’s four preferred securities, with 99.3% of votes cast supporting the changes.

The amendments cover STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD, replacing existing semi-monthly or quarterly payment schedules with distributions every business day. Dividends will continue to accrue over weekends and holidays, while annual dividend rates remain unchanged.

Strategy expects STRC to begin daily payments on Nov. 2, followed by the other three securities on Jan. 4, 2027. The company said the shorter payment cycle could improve liquidity and reduce price fluctuations in its preferred shares.

The securities currently offer annual dividend rates ranging from 8% to 12%. STRC carries a variable rate of 12%, while the remaining three offer fixed rates.

The move follows similar efforts by rival Bitcoin treasury company Strive, which introduced daily dividends on its SATA preferred stock in June. Strive also recently raised $630 million through a second preferred offering, SATS, which carries a 15% annual dividend rate.

Strategy remains the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,517 BTC, compared with Strive’s 43,000 BTC.

Coinbase denies systems breach, says vendor exposed customer data

Some Coinbase customers’ contact information was exposed in a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude, the exchange said Wednesday.

The incident impacted a “small subset” of Coinbase customers, along with other Amplitude clients, Coinbase Support said on X.

Coinbase denied that its own systems had been breached and said customer funds were not affected.

The disclosure adds to Wednesday’s reports of cyberattacks affecting both crypto exchanges and traditional financial firms. In South Korea, Bithumb is investigating whether a breach of its internal work platform exposed customer information, while brokerage Daishin Securities reported a leak of personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers.

Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says uncertainty over the longevity of US tokenization rules could prevent investors from committing substantial assets to tokenized markets, despite the securities regulator opening a temporary path for onchain stock trading this year. 

Speaking during Robinhood’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Tenev welcomed the SEC’s innovation exemption but said further rulemaking or legislation would be needed to provide longer-term regulatory certainty. 

“As far as the innovation exemption goes, I think it’s a really positive step... I do think more needs to be done to give people a little bit of certainty because as we talk to customers, I think the uncertainty of what happens in five years is likely to be an impediment to, like, putting serious assets onto this technology.”

Tokenized stock offerings have faced resistance from traditional issuers. Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs were among 16 companies that objected to their shares being offered on the proposed OKXICE venue, while AMC CEO Adam Aron separately criticized Robinhood’s tokenized stock products.

title: Coinbase Denies Platform Intrusion as Vendor Data Leak Emerges
summary: Coinbase is facing fresh security questions after a breach at analytics provider Amplitude exposed customer contact information, while unverified claims put the number of affected users above 70,000. The exchange insists its own systems and customer funds remain untouched. Coinbase Denies Direct Bre...
content:
Coinbase is facing fresh security questions after a breach at analytics provider Amplitude exposed customer contact information, while unverified claims put the number of affected users above 70,000. The exchange insists its own systems and customer funds remain untouched.

Key Takeaways

  • The Coinbase Support X account confirmed an Amplitude vendor incident but denied any unauthorized access to its systems.
  • Claims that more than 70,000 Coinbase users were affected remain unverified.
  • Coinbase faces renewed questions about third-party security following its costly 2025 incident.

Coinbase Denies Direct Breach as 70,000-User Claim Circulates

This week, Coinbase acknowledged a security incident involving Amplitude, a third-party analytics provider that processes customer information. The disclosure followed allegations circulating on X that attackers had obtained contact details belonging to more than 70,000 Coinbase users.

Alongside this, Coinbase rejected suggestions that its infrastructure had been breached, drawing a firm distinction between compromised vendor data and unauthorized access to its trading platform. The centralized exchange (CEX) platform‘s X account stated:

“Coinbase has not had a data breach. Amplitude, an analytics vendor, experienced a security incident which impacted a small subset of Coinbase customer contact data, among other Amplitude customers. We’ve found no evidence of unauthorized access to Coinbase systems, and customer funds were not impacted. We are notifying impacted customers and regulatory agencies in accordance with our legal obligations.”

The company has not disclosed how many customers were affected, what specific information was exposed, or how attackers gained access. Accounts, including Delcrxpto and Slowmist security executive 23pds, circulated the 70,000-user figure, which remains unverified at press time.

Third-Party Exposure Raises Phishing Concerns

Amplitude provides analytics technology that helps businesses measure customer engagement and interactions with digital products. Such arrangements can expose information outside a company’s primary infrastructure when a vendor experiences a security failure. Secondary accounts identified email addresses and telephone numbers as potentially compromised information, although Coinbase has not independently confirmed those specific fields.

No compromise of passwords, private keys, recovery phrases, or account balances has been reported. Nevertheless, exposed contact information can furnish scammers with material for targeted phishing campaigns, so-called wrench attacks, fraudulent customer-support calls and SIM-swap attempts. The distinction is consequential. Criminals don’t necessarily need access to an exchange’s servers to impersonate its representatives and persuade customers to surrender credentials. Coinbase said it is notifying affected customers and regulators as required.

Previous Contractor Breach Cost Coinbase Hundreds of Millions

The disclosure follows a substantially more damaging contractor-related incident uncovered in May 2025, when bribed customer-support personnel working for Taskus improperly accessed sensitive information belonging to 69,461 Coinbase users. That specific episode involved personal identification records, financial information, and limited transaction histories.

Attackers demanded $20 million, which Coinbase refused to pay, while remediation expenses and related costs reached hundreds of millions of dollars. The latest incident appears considerably narrower, with no reported loss of customer assets or intrusion into Coinbase systems. Its timing also puts the exchange under scrutiny ahead of third-quarter earnings scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 29.

For now, Coinbase has offered assurances about its systems but little detail about the vendor intrusion itself. The unanswered question is how much customer information left Amplitude’s control, and who now possesses it.

title: Sam Bankman-Fried wrote to actor portraying him in Netflix series
summary: The former FTX CEO remains incarcerated as Irish actor Anthony Boyle portrays him in a series about the downfall of the crypto exchange and his relationship with Caroline Ellison.
content:
In about three weeks, Netflix is set to release one of the first dramatizations of the saga of cryptocurrency exchange FTX since its CEO, Sam “SBF” Bankman-Fried, was found guilty and sentenced to prison.

According to a Wednesday Vanity Fair report, Anthony Boyle, the Irish actor portraying SBF on screen for the Netflix series ‘The Altruists,’ contacted the former CEO in prison via email as he prepared for the role. Although Boyle said he “promised him that I wouldn’t divulge anything,” Bankman-Fried reportedly answered the bulk of the actor’s questions ahead of the series’ release.

“I was interested in what possessed someone to become the world’s youngest billionaire,” said Boyle, according to Vanity Fair. “I’m not really interested in money or crypto or finance. It was: What makes them do the things that they do?”

Based on a trailer Netflix released on Oct. 8, the series appeared to be centered on the relationship between Bankman-Fried and his colleague and girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, who headed FTX’s sister arm, Alameda Research. SBF was convicted of seven felony counts related to the misuse of customer funds at FTX and sentenced to 25 years in prison, while Ellison was released in January after serving more than a year as part of a plea deal with US authorities.

Former FTX COO Constance Wang said that the on-screen portrayal of the executives made her “feel physically upset,” adding that SBF was more “socially awkward” than Boyle demonstrated.

Bankman-Fried has already been covered by several media outlets and was the subject of Michael Lewis’ 2023 book Going Infinite. Ben McKenzie’s documentary Everyone Is Lying to You for Money included a 2022 interview with the former CEO before the exchange’s downfall, but no other significant dramatization of SBF or FTX has been released on the big screen or television until The Altruists.

title: XTB's Quarterly Profit Quadruples and Beats Forecasts as Clients Trade Less
summary:

content:
2026-10-28T21:00:18.087+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 19:00 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The PLN 213.7 million result topped the analyst average by 6.4% but was less than half the second quarter's.
  • Revenue rose 66% as the broker made almost twice as much per lot, mostly on gold, oil and gas contracts.

XTB's third-quarter net profit rose fourfold from a year earlier to PLN 213.7 million (about $54 million), the Warsaw-listed broker said today (Wednesday). The preliminary figure came in 6.4% above the PLN 200.8 million average of five analyst forecasts.

That is still less than half the PLN 492.2 million XTB earned in the second quarter, a drop analysts had expected as markets calmed.

Revenue rose 65.9% year on year to PLN 623.3 million, although clients traded 18.3% fewer contracts for difference (CFDs) measured in lots. XTB earned PLN 301 per lot, almost double the PLN 152 of a year earlier, as commodity CFDs produced 70.8% of its gross result on financial instruments.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The comparison base was weak. A year ago XTB's profit fell 74% to PLN 53.2 million and revenue dropped 20% on low market volatility.

Revenue Grew Faster Than at London-Listed Rivals

Of the three listed CFD providers that have reported the July-September quarter, XTB posted the fastest revenue growth.

IG Group expects revenue about 14% lower year on year after it kept a smaller share of client trading as income, while Plus500's revenue rose 11% to $203.2 million and it raised its full-year outlook.

XTB's growth was about six times Plus500's, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, though its revenue was still 37.2% below the PLN 992.3 million of a second quarter in which profit beat forecasts and the shares hit a record.

Gold, Oil and Gas Carried the Trading Result

XTB said the quarter brought less activity on financial and commodity markets than the first half, with volatility staying high in commodities and markets calmer on stock indices.

The slowdown had started earlier. XTB's average monthly trading volume fell 26% in the second quarter from the first, according to FM Intelligence's Broker Volumes data.

Commodity CFDs, led by gold, crude oil, natural gas and silver, generated 70.8% of the gross result on financial instruments, against 48.5% a year earlier. That share was 60.5% in the second quarter, FM Intelligence data show.

Index CFDs fell to 12.0% from 32.4%. Stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs), grouped as other instruments, rose to 12.3% from 8.3%.

More Clients, Higher Marketing Bill

XTB added 335,704 new clients in the quarter, up 51.4% from a year earlier and slightly more than the 333,292 of the second quarter. Its client base reached 3.14 million, while active clients rose 70.3% to 1.57 million.

Net deposits rose to PLN 5.65 billion from PLN 3.23 billion a year earlier, the company said.

Operating costs increased 23.2% year on year to PLN 397.6 million, mainly because marketing spending rose by PLN 45.8 million to PLN 187.3 million. Costs fell by PLN 22.1 million from the second quarter as online marketing was cut.

The next push began after the quarter closed. XTB started what it calls its biggest advertising campaign on October 1, featuring footballer Zlatan Ibrahimović and boxer Tyson Fury on four continents.

The company said it signed up more than 100,600 new clients in the first 27 days of October, against its goal of an average of 250,000 to 290,000 a quarter in 2026. It still expects 2026 operating costs up to about 30% higher than in 2025, with marketing up about 50%.

Nine-Month Profit Nearly Double All of 2025

For the first nine months, net profit reached PLN 1.24 billion, against PLN 463.3 million a year earlier and PLN 644.2 million for all of 2025. The first half had already brought a record 703,333 new clients, though CFDs generated 96% of the trading result.

The Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF) said in August that its review of how firms sell CFDs to Polish clients was still open.

XTB will discuss the figures at a results conference tomorrow (Thursday) and publish its full quarterly report on November 20.

title: Jason Calacanis’ Bleak Bitcoin Prediction Draws $3M in Rival Bets—but He Won’t Bite
summary: Three bitcoin investors have thrown down $1 million challenges to Jason Calacanis after he declared the cryptocurrency would never reclaim its record high. One offered a decade-long wager, the other just two years, but Calacanis wants a shorter contest. Adding to the stakes, Hollywood producer and b...
content:
Three bitcoin investors have thrown down $1 million challenges to Jason Calacanis after he declared the cryptocurrency would never reclaim its record high. One offered a decade-long wager, the other just two years, but Calacanis wants a shorter contest. Adding to the stakes, Hollywood producer and bitcoin educator Terence Michael entered the fray.

Key Takeaways

  • Jason Calacanis’ bleak bitcoin prediction has sparked a high-stakes confrontation with prominent investors.
  • Fred Krueger is challenging Calacanis to put serious money behind his controversial bitcoin forecast.
  • Grant Cardone has entered the dispute with a competing proposal, adding another twist to the debate.

Fred Krueger Offers $1 Million on Bitcoin’s Future

Bitcoin investor Fred Krueger challenged technology investor Jason Calacanis to a $1 million wager after the All-In podcast co-host declared bitcoin would never establish another all-time high. Krueger opened his challenge by repeating Calacanis’ prediction, “Bitcoin will never break its all-time high again,” before firing back, “Jason, I’ll bet you $1,000,000 that you’re wrong.”

His proposal gives bitcoin until Oct. 28, 2036, to exceed $126,210.50, its October 2025 peak. Both participants would deposit $1 million into independent escrow, using a mutually agreed custodian and objective price oracle. Krueger spelled out the financial stakes: “If bitcoin does, I win $1 million. If it doesn’t, you win $1 million.” The wager would settle immediately upon a new record or expire after 10 years.

Krueger concluded his challenge with a pointed reminder of Calacanis’ sweeping prediction. “No excuses. No moving the goalposts. You said NEVER. I’m giving you just 10 years. Do we have a bet?” The proposal effectively asks Calacanis to put a seven-figure sum behind his conviction that bitcoin’s record-setting days are permanently over.

Calacanis Wants a 12-Month Wager Instead

Calacanis responded with a considerably shorter proposition, writing, “Propose next 12 month bet”. That response drew fire from observers who questioned why someone predicting bitcoin would never reclaim its peak would restrict the wager to a single year. One critic remarked, “Goal posts immediately moved,” while another was less charitable, responding, “So your statement was complete bullsh** then.”

Calacanis’ latest forecast claims that bitcoin could revisit $57,000 within 12 months, citing exchange-traded fund (ETF) outflows and competition from artificial intelligence (AI) investments. His prediction of a permanent ceiling, however, extends well beyond that near-term bearish forecast, creating a distinction between his original declaration and the narrower wager he appears willing to entertain.

Grant Cardone Offers a Second Million-Dollar Challenge

Alongside Krueger, BTC proponent Grant Cardone entered the fray with another $1 million proposition, this time allowing bitcoin just two years to reclaim its record. Like Krueger, Cardone repeated Calacanis’ declaration, “Bitcoin will never break its all-time high again,” before issuing his own offer: “Jason, I’ll bet you $1,000,000 it will break its ATH.”

Cardone specified the terms, writing, “Bitcoin hits or exceeds $126,210.50 on or before October 28, 2028, 12PM PST”. He also offered flexible payment arrangements, stating, “I’m happy to trust you to pay or if you prefer we can each escrow the dollars with independent party.” He added, “The bet is either settled when bitcoin hits the ATH or on October 28, 2028,” before asking, “Jason do we have a bet?”

Hollywood Producer Terence Michael Ups the Ante

After Cardone’s offer, Terence Michael, a Hollywood producer turned bitcoin educator, added another $1 million to the table. “Hey Jason … want an easy $3 million? I agree to the same terms as Grant just offered you (below). Add [Fred Krueger’s] original bet to the mix and you have $3M saying ‘bitcoin is dead’ is free. Let’s see if you have conviction,” Michael wrote, sharing Cardone’s X post.

At the time of writing at 2:55 p.m. Eastern time on Wednesday, Calacanis had not responded to Cardone’s or Michael’s challenge. Three investors have now offered seven-figure wagers against the same prediction, with deadlines eight years apart.

The lingering contradiction is difficult to ignore: declaring bitcoin will never reach another record is one proposition, but betting it won’t happen within the next 12 months is an entirely different one.

title: 001k.bot Introduces 0% Service Fee on Swaps Between USDT and BTC
summary: Kyiv, Ukraine, 28th October 2026, Chainwire

Kyiv, Ukraine, 28th October 2026, Chainwire

Kyiv, Ukraine, October 28th, 2026, Chainwire

001k.bot has launched a promotion on USDT and BTC swaps in both directions: the service fee on USDT → BTC and BTC → USDT market swaps is 0%. The offer suits those who prefer to spread their BTC purchases across several transactions to avoid making decisions on emotion, as well as those who need to swap BTC back into USDT.

This format works especially well for those who prefer to buy BTC gradually rather than convert the full amount in one go. For example, $5,000 can be split into several transactions, with the timing of each next purchase left up to the user. Under the promotion, 001k.bot charges no service fee on these market swaps. The same terms apply when selling: if a user needs to move part of their funds from BTC back into stablecoins, no service fee is charged on that swap either.

Before confirming a transaction, the user sees the current rate, the service fee, and the final amount they will receive, so they can assess the swap terms in advance and compare them with other platforms.

This approach does not eliminate market risk or guarantee a better price or profit, but it makes it possible to spread the purchase over time and keep part of the funds in USDT.

“It’s impossible to time the entry point, so the professional approach is to split the purchase into parts. We removed the service fee on USDT/BTC and BTC/USDT market swaps so that splitting a purchase doesn’t create additional service costs,” says Serhii Hutsu, brand ambassador at 001k.bot.

001k.bot also offers a breakdown of a historical BTC model that identifies the period from October 2026 to early February 2027 as a potential window for gradual accumulation. The model serves only as a reference point: it does not forecast an exact price or date for the low, and it does not guarantee a subsequent rise in BTC.

0% Service Fee Terms

The promotion applies to the 001k.bot service fee on USDT/BTC market swaps covered by the promotion terms in both directions: USDT → BTC and BTC → USDT.

The spread may be included in the quote. BTC withdrawals and Limit Order transactions are charged separately under the service’s current terms.

Buying or selling BTC in a few steps

The offer is available in the 001k.bot Telegram and on the web platform. To buy, select the USDT/BTC swap, enter the amount, check the rate and the final amount of BTC, then confirm the transaction. To sell, the steps are the same: select the BTC/USDT swap, enter the amount, check the rate and the final amount of USDT, then confirm the transaction.

Purchased BTC is credited to the 001k.bot balance, where it can be kept or withdrawn to an external wallet via the Bitcoin network. Users who have already completed verification do not need to go through KYC again. New users need to create an account, complete KYC, and top up their balance with USDT or BTC.

Current promotion dates, the rate, and full terms are displayed right before the transaction is confirmed.

About 001k.bot

001k.bot is a crypto-financial platform designed for fast asset management, exchanges, and payments. It offers fast swaps at the best market rates, limit orders, off-chain transactions, secure asset storage, and a multi-level referral program.

Originally launched as a Telegram bot, 001k.bot is now available as a full-featured, independent web platform that works in any browser — no apps or messengers required.

title: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks
summary: The largest Bitcoin treasury company will begin daily dividend payments on STRC in November, with three other preferred securities following in January 2027.
content:
Bitcoin treasury company Strategy said Wednesday that shareholders approved amendments allowing its four preferred stocks to pay daily dividends, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor, according to preliminary results.

The amendments cover Strategy’s four preferred securities — STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD — shifting dividend payments from semi-monthly or quarterly schedules to every business day. Dividends will accrue daily, including weekends and holidays, without changing their annual dividend rates.

Strategy expects daily payments on STRC to begin Nov. 2, with STRF, STRK and STRD following on Jan. 4, 2027. Strategy said the changes are designed to shorten the time between earning dividends and receiving cash, while supporting liquidity and price stability in its preferred shares.

Source: Michael Saylor

Strategy’s preferred stocks carry annual dividend rates ranging from 8% to 12%, with STRC offering a variable rate currently set at 12%. The other three securities pay fixed dividends, while STRK also gives investors the option to convert their holdings into Strategy common stock.

Related: Strategy skips Bitcoin purchases, spends $205M on STRC buybacks

Strive expands daily dividend offerings with $630 million raise

Fellow Bitcoin treasury company Strive introduced daily cash dividends on its SATA preferred stock in June, months ahead of Strategy’s planned changes. The company has since launched a second preferred security, SATS, offering a fixed 15% annual dividend rate, with daily payments scheduled to begin Nov. 9, subject to declaration.

Strive closed a $630 million SATS offering on Oct. 20, selling 7 million shares at $90 each. The company said proceeds could be used for Bitcoin purchases and other corporate purposes, but has not disclosed how much it intends to allocate to the cryptocurrency.

Strategy remains the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,517 BTC, while Strive ranks fourth with 43,000 BTC, according to BitcoinTreasuries.net data.
