title: Centralized Exchange and DeFi Losses Dominate 2026 Crypto Hacks Despite Hardware Wallet Failures
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Centralized Exchange and DeFi Losses Dominate 2026 Crypto Hacks Despite Hardware Wallet Failures
Lightning.news data shared with Bitcoin Magazine puts net 2026 crypto hack losses at roughly $2.35 billion after freezes and returns. September alone accounted for about $768 million, l...
content:
Crypto hacks have produced roughly $2.35 billion in net losses so far in 2026 after freezes and returns, according to a report by Lightning.news shared with Bitcoin Magazine. A security researcher by the name of Stacy Muur posted on X compiled “a list of protocols that were hacked for more than $50,000 in 2026.” 230 protocols year-to-date. “Crypto security is absolutely cooked.” September alone accounted for about $768 million in Muur’s tally, driven mainly by centralized exchanges and DeFi rather than pure Bitcoin self-custody hardware wallets, which got significant news coverage at the time.

The largest single loss was Bitget’s September 24 drain of roughly $387.5 million from hot and warm wallets. The exchange and firms including Chainalysis, Elliptic, and TRM Labs have linked the incident to North Korea, citing IP patterns consistent with prior DPRK-linked VPN use, on-chain overlaps with wallets tied to earlier Lazarus Group and TraderTraitor activity, including the 2025 Bybit theft. Attackers used third-party security products to inject fraudulent withdrawal commands without taking private keys.

Liquid Network, Blockstream’s Bitcoin sidechain, took the next-largest hit when attackers exploited an Elements software bug in early September to mint about 4,000 unbacked L-BTC and peg them out for roughly 4,000 real bitcoins, valued near $320 million at the time. The self-described white-hat actors returned 3,400 BTC after negotiations conducted on-chain via OP_RETURN messages and kept about 600 BTC. No federation keys were compromised. The loss came from a type of inflation bug on the Liquid network protocol. 

Samson Mow later called the episode part of an “avalanche of AI-assisted attacks” that had already reached other Bitcoin-adjacent software before hitting Liquid. The network is back and running now, having covered the losses, presumably from investors. 

DeFi platforms showed the same pattern of concentrated, high-value losses. Drift Protocol lost approximately $285–296 million in an April governance and multisig compromise that involved months of social engineering. An investigation commissioned by the project attributed the operation to North Korean actors. 

KelpDAO’s LayerZero-powered rsETH bridge was drained of roughly $292 million in unbacked tokens after a single-verifier design was subverted. LayerZero stated that preliminary indicators pointed to DPRK’s Lazarus Group, specifically TraderTraitor. 

Tectonic on Cronos saw about $120.4 million borrowed against manipulated collateral in late August. Validators later rewound the chain and recovered the majority, though several million dollars that had already been bridged off-network were not restored.

Incidents involving Bitcoin hardware wallets were smaller in aggregate despite the wide news coverage. Galaxy Research placed the Coinkite RNG hack values in the range of roughly 1,596–1,789 BTC, on the order of $100–130 million, with higher upper-bound estimates near 2,055 BTC. 

Ledger losses of roughly $86–102 million traced to devices sold through the authorized Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, where an unauthorized hardware implant captured recovery phrases during setup, a supply chain attack. The company stated that confirmed cases were limited to that reseller’s supply chain and that its own systems and direct sales were unaffected, though there are unconfirmed reports of such bugged devices making it to German markets. Combined, however, these hardware-adjacent events remain well below the single largest CEX and DeFi incidents. 

The year has also coincided with the practical deployment of AI coding agents capable of scanning codebases for vulnerabilities and automating exploit development. Muur has stated that “AI is definitely making it much easier to find and exploit bugs. I think we’re entering a pretty serious cybersecurity arms race.” 

Reports note that code-flaw exploits accelerated after the February release of models such as GPT-5.3-Codex and Claude Opus 4.6, which showed high success rates on smart-contract bug benchmarks at low cost. 

OpenAI has disclosed internal testing cases in which agents accessed unauthorized test-network funds or bypassed controls to complete tasks. Most of the year’s largest heists still relied on traditional vectors such as key compromise, social engineering, and infrastructure flaws, but the lowered barrier for discovering and weaponizing bugs adds a new layer of risk, particularly for complex smart-contract systems and sidechains.

Bitcoin’s base layer itself has not been the source of these losses. The bulk of the 2026 damage has concentrated in CEX hot-wallet infrastructure, DeFi governance, oracle designs, and Bitcoin sidechain code, while pure self-custody hardware wallets, even when imperfect, have accounted for a distinctly smaller share. Nevertheless, calls for an update to self custody recommendations have emerged from industry leaders, pushing forward multivendor multisig wallets as the future of niche industry.

title: Google Debuting a Bank-Grade Crypto Custody Tool Built on Split Keys: Report
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Google Debuting a Bank-Grade Crypto Custody Tool Built on Split Keys: Report
Google is previewing a crypto custody system that splits private keys across separate environments, with several banks testing it ahead of a planned early 2027 launch.
This post Google Debuting a Bank-Grad...
content:
Google is reportedly unveiling Google Multi-Party Compute, a crypto custody system that splits signing keys across separate systems, at its first digital assets symposium in New York today. The product is in private preview with several financial institutions. Alphabet has started using it to secure its own assets, according to CoinDesk reporting.

Google plans commercial availability in early 2027 and has not disclosed pricing.

The system applies multi-party computation to a signing key. The key is divided into fragments held by separate parties or machines, and a transaction requires a set number of fragments to sign. 

The full key is never assembled in one place. A bank could hold one share on its own hardware, another in Google Cloud, and a third with a rival cloud provider. Institutions can set thresholds such as two-of-three or five-of-seven. Before any signature, a policy engine running inside Google’s Confidential Space checks the transfer against limits, destination restrictions, and approval rules. 

Google says it has no access to key shares in unencrypted form, per CoinDesk.

Crypto’s security issues

The pitch rests on a persistent problem. Chainalysis attributed 43.8% of cryptocurrency stolen in 2024 to compromised private keys. DeFiLlama data shows roughly 40% of the $16.69 billion lost to hacks through June came from key compromises. In June, an attacker took seven keys from one developer’s computer during the Humanity Protocol breach and drained wallets across two networks. 

Such incidents show how concentrated signing authority creates a single point of failure. The industry has responded by recommending multi-vendor multisignature setups that spread control across hardware and software providers.

Google also frames the product against AI-enabled fraud. Chainalysis found that scams linked to AI tool vendors averaged $3.2 million per operation in 2025, compared with $719,000 for other scams. The report links the two figures but does not prove that AI caused the difference. 

Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has warned that AI could eventually find mathematical shortcuts that weaken wallet signatures. No AI system has shown that capability. Google’s MPC design targets stolen credentials and unauthorized transfers, not a break in the underlying cryptography.

Quantum computing presents a separate, longer-term risk. Google researchers estimated that a sufficiently powerful future machine could derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in about nine minutes. Roughly 6.9 million bitcoin have exposed public keys. Google says its architecture can adopt post-quantum signatures later without forcing institutions to rebuild their systems, but it has set no timetable. Background on how quantum machines threaten bitcoin explains which addresses are most exposed.

Google enters a market led by Fireblocks, Fordefi, and BitGo. Google argued to CoinDesk that its banking relationships and security expertise give it an advantage. It also positions itself as a neutral supplier for banks that do not want to rely on competitors. 

Banks already use specialized platforms, such as BNP Paribas’s custody work with Metaco, and multi-institution vaults built with BitGo.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto PAC spending before midterms possibly obscured after reported FEC hack
summary: The FEC reported an “electronic filing system outage” on Tuesday as groups are expected to ramp up spending before the US midterm elections.
content:
The US Federal Election Commission (FEC) filing system is offline after reports of a hack, potentially obscuring expenditures by super political action committees (PACs) and other groups in the final days before the 2026 midterm elections.

As of Tuesday at 7:48 pm UTC, the FEC said it was continuing to experience an “electronic filing system outage,” but was working to resolve the issue. Campaign finance data by PACs and other entities were still available for the public to view, but the system outage suggested that last-minute spending could go unreported.

For example, with just six days until Election Day, FEC filings showed no expenditures from the cryptocurrency industry-aligned Super PACs Fairshake, Defend American Jobs, Protect Progress, Fellowship and Digital Freedom Fund since Sunday. Cointelegraph reached out to Fairshake for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

Super PACs are required to report certain spending to the FEC within 24 hours of the funds being used, provided the expenditures total $1,000 or more. Candidates for House and Senate seats, likewise, are expected to report contributions of $1,000 or more within 48 hours in the 20 days before an election.

Digital Freedom Fund, a PAC launched by Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, reported on Sunday that it had spent more than $572,000 on text messages to support various Republican Senate candidates, with the majority going to bolster Ken Paxton’s campaign in Texas. Protect Progress’ most recent expenditure before the FEC outage showed more than $50,000 for a direct mail campaign supporting Representative Aisha Wahab in California’s 14th district.

Related: CLARITY vote failure could stoke more crypto PAC spending in key races

The 2026 midterms could be consequential for many in the crypto industry who support digital asset laws passing in Congress and state-level legislation and policies. Lawmakers in Congress failed to advance a crypto market structure bill in September, leading to Fairshake and other industry advocates supporting the reelection of those who voted in favor of the legislation.

Reuters reported on Tuesday that the disruption was caused by the FEC website being targeted by a hacker or hackers, according to an email. An FEC spokesperson told Cointelegraph that its IT staff were ”actively working to restore service.”

History repeats itself in Ohio with crypto PAC spending on Senate candidates

In 2024, Fairshake spent about $41 million opposing Senator Sherrod Brown’s reelection bid against Republican Bernie Moreno. The Democratic lawmaker ended up losing his Senate seat, but announced that he would run against incumbent Jon Husted in 2026, leading to another election with money from the crypto industry flowing into attack ads.

Before the FEC outage, Fairshake reported spending $56 million on media to oppose Brown and support Husted, while the Digital Freedom Fund disclosed more than $7 million in expenditures for the same race. The crypto PACs are just some of the groups interested in influencing Ohio voters in the 2026 midterms, with reports of tens of millions of dollars being spent from Democratic- and Republican-aligned organizations.

title: Bitcoin price bounce rejected at 50-day trend line ahead of FOMC, earnings
summary: Bitcoin failed to move past its 50-day simple moving average as market participants awaited the outcome of the FOMC meeting and key tech earnings.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) gave back early gains around Wednesday’s Wall Street open as markets prepared for the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin fell around 0.3% on Wednesday after upside volatility failed to sustain past $81,687.
  • US stock markets tracked sideways into the run-up to the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) interest-rate decision and press conference after South Korea’s KOSPI gained 6.6%.
  • BTC/USD stalled below its 50-day simple moving average at $81,831, which acted as local resistance.

US stocks tread water as focus turns to Fed chair Warsh

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD failing to break beyond $81,700, instead reversing to as low as $80,297 on Bitstamp. At the time of writing, the pair was down 0.3% on the day.

US stocks opened flat ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting statement and press conference from Fed chair Kevin Warsh. Markets overwhelmingly expected officials to hold rates in their current 3.75-4% range, with the focus instead on Warsh’s language and comments on the economy.

Data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed 90.6% odds of a pause at Wednesday’s FOMC, while the outcome for the December meeting remained a 0.25% rate hike.

Fed target-rate probabilities (screenshot). Source: CME Group

Commenting, Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, saw Warsh’s words potentially shifting the December odds. Between the two meetings, traders would be digesting the result of the US midterm elections on Nov. 3.

“Markets may have priced in no rate change, but they haven’t priced in the election outcome,” he summarized on Tuesday.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index did not follow South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index higher after the KOSPI closed up 6.6%, its best daily gain since July.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

In his latest commentary, data analyst Charl van Zyl suggested that the Fed move and the week’s key tech earnings data would materially influence market views of the health of the AI sector.

“Even after a nearly 10% two-day bounce, the index is still 34% below its June 22 record of 9,115. On Monday it closed 40% below that peak,” he noted of the index.

BTC price gains capped by 50-day moving average

After BTC price upside momentum faded, the 50-day simple moving average (SMA) at $81,831 functioned as resistance on low time frames.

Related: Bitcoin price analysis sees ‘strong rally’ as old coins become dormant

“A 4H close below $80,565 reduces the probability of retesting resistance at the 50-Day SMA,” Alan commented.

BTC/USD four-hour chart with 50-day SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Analyzing exchange order-book liquidity, onchain analytics platform Glassnode flagged bid liquidity moving further below $80,000, shifting the likely reversal area lower should downside accelerate.

“Only $3.4M in bids remains at $80K. The bids have moved down to $78K-79K, where orders add up to about $42M, up from about $24M in mid-October,” it wrote in the latest edition of its weekly newsletter, The Week Onchain.

“That is the largest block of bids near price, and the first place where we would expect buyers to step in on a dip.”

Bitcoin order-book liquidity heatmap (Binance). Source: Glassnode

title: Phantom launches Kalshi-powered prediction markets for US users
summary: The crypto wallet’s new integration offers CFTC-regulated event contracts through Kalshi, as prediction markets face growing legal challenges in the US.
content:
Crypto wallet provider Phantom has launched prediction markets for eligible US users through an integration with Kalshi, allowing them to trade on crypto prices, sports and other real-world events directly within its app.

According to Wednesday’s announcement, the integration offers CFTC-regulated event contracts, including short-term Bitcoin price markets that settle every 15 minutes. Trades can be funded through Phantom Cash balances, denominated in the CASH stablecoin.

Kalshi handles customer verification, account management and trade execution, while Phantom provides access through its app. The launch follows no-action relief granted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in March, allowing Phantom to connect users to regulated markets without registering as an introducing broker, subject to certain conditions.

The service is rolling out through a new Predict tab in Phantom, with availability varying by state and market category. Eligible US users can view live market data, sports scores and market discussions before placing trades through an interface similar to a cryptocurrency token swap.

Related: Pentagon bans US forces from using military info to bet in prediction markets

Kalshi’s legal battles continue as trading volumes rise

Phantom’s entry into prediction markets comes amid a widening legal dispute over the industry in the US. On Monday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah after the state challenged Kalshi’s event contracts under its gambling laws, adding to a series of cases over whether federal derivatives regulation supersedes state gambling laws.

Despite the legal uncertainty, trading activity continues to grow. Kalshi recorded $10.8 billion in crypto contract volume over the 30 days ending Oct. 27, up 19.6% from the previous period, according to data compiled by DeFi Rate.

Kalshi trading volume and market share from Sept. 28 to Oct. 27, 2026. Source: DeFi Rate

summary:
Google Cloud is
developing a cryptocurrency custody service for financial institutions that
distributes transaction-signing authority across multiple systems. The product
is in private preview, with commercial availability planned for early 2027.
London's trading industry is coming home!
Other finan...
content:
2026-10-28T18:21:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 16:21 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Alphabet is using MPC technology to secure digital assets on Ethereum and Solana, without disclosing their value.
  • Bitcoin controls added rules on 1 October to assess transaction amounts and identify destination addresses.

Google Cloud is developing a cryptocurrency custody service for financial institutions that distributes transaction-signing authority across multiple systems. The product is in private preview, with commercial availability planned for early 2027.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Other financial firms are also developing digital asset services for institutional clients. Spotex connected its trading venue to BitGo's custody and settlement infrastructure, while Virtu Financial joined BitGo Prime's liquidity network.

JPMorgan has also planned to accept Bitcoin and Ether as loan collateral for institutional clients, using a third-party custodian. Ripple partnered with South Africa's Absa Bank to provide digital asset custody technology.

Called Google Multi-Party Compute, the service is designed to help institutions secure and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenised assets without storing a complete private key in one place.

Google Cloud's documentation describes MPC as a key management service that allows separate parties to sign blockchain transactions collaboratively. The product remains in preview, with support potentially limited.

Google Expands Bitcoin Transaction Controls

Google updated the service's documentation on Monday, ahead of its MPC Symposium in New York on Wednesday. The event focuses on the company's MPC technology and research. Speakers include representatives from Morgan Stanley, OKX, Citi and Wells Fargo.

Google's release notes show that the service has received several updates since August. On 1 October, the company added rules to evaluate Bitcoin transaction amounts, identify destination address types and detect change outputs. The update also introduced support for authorising Bitcoin transactions through its policy engine.

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) October 28, 2026

The service builds on Google's earlier work in multi-party computation. In 2023, the company published guidance on using its Confidential Space infrastructure to develop systems for securing digital assets.

Alphabet Also Uses the Technology

Several financial institutions are testing the service, according to CoinDesk. Alphabet is also using it to secure digital assets on Ethereum and Solana, though Google has not disclosed the assets or their value.

The service combines transaction signing, policy controls and key recovery. Google plans commercial availability in early 2027 but has not announced pricing or a launch date.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Four Preferred Stocks
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Four Preferred Stocks
Strategy (MSTR) shareholders approved paying daily dividends on four of its preferred stocks.
This post Strategy (MSTR) Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Four Preferred Stocks first appeared on Bitc...
content:
Strategy shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment, the company announced Wednesday. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor, according to Executive Chairman Michael Saylor.

The amendment allows STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day, including weekends and holidays.

The proposal surfaced on September 25, when the company asked holders to attend a special meeting on October 28. Strategy said the change “would reduce reinvestment lag, enhance liquidity and market efficiency, and increase price stability.”

At the time Strategy said that they “believe these enhancements can also benefit our common stockholders by increasing the attractiveness and utility of our Digital Credit instruments, supporting our ability to access preferred equity capital efficiently and expanding the capital markets toolkit we use to execute our Bitcoin Treasury strategy.

Under the approved structure, dividends accrue every day but are paid on the next business day. Strategy has said scheduled dividend rates and total dividend obligations remain unchanged. The company has argued the change could benefit common stockholders by making its Digital Credit instruments easier to use and easier to fund.

The timing depends on board action. If the board approves the change and required filings are completed, the first STRC record and payment dates would fall on November 1 and 2, 2026. For STRF, STRK and STRD, the first record and payment dates would be January 1 and 4, 2027. Those dates also depend on operational readiness.

STRC pays a variable rate that the company can change at its discretion. Its rate for the month ended June 30, 2026 was 11.50%, according to Strategy’s quarterly report. Shareholders approved moving STRC to semi-monthly payments in June, and the new amendment builds on that precedent.

In short, STRC is designed to help Strategy raise money from investors through a preferred stock offering targeting a stable $100 price and a variable dividend yield, then use that capital to continuously buy Bitcoin regardless of its short-term price movements. This creates a potential global dollar-cost-averaging machine for Bitcoin.

Final vote certification will come in a company filing. Board action remains the final step before any new payment schedule begins.

Strategy’s bitcoin moves this year 

The vote comes after bitcoin fell into somewhat of a bear market. Strategy slowed its bitcoin purchases this year and sold some holdings to fund preferred dividends, interest payments and repurchases. 

The company’s common stock, MSTR, is down near 50% over the past year, though it has risen by a figure approaching 1,000% since Strategy began buying bitcoin in 2020.

Earlier this week, Strategy said they paused Bitcoin purchases for the prior week and maintained its holdings at 848,517 BTC, acquired for $64.02 billion at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin. 

The company spent $204.9 million repurchasing STRC preferred stock while retaining a $4.83 billion cash reserve. 

Fellow bitcoin-treasury company Strive pays cash dividends on its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA) every business day. This started on June 16, after moving from monthly payments. 

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Target to $1.6 Million as Institutions Keep Buying
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Target to $1.6 Million as Institutions Keep Buying
Bitwise raised its 2036 bitcoin price target to $1.6 million, projecting 34.3% annual growth on institutional demand and fixed supply.
This post Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Target to $1.6 Million as Institutions K...
content:
Bitwise Asset Management this week released its 2027 Bitcoin Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, raising its 2036 base-case price target for bitcoin to $1,599,766 from $1.3 million a year earlier. 

The forecast implies a 34.3% compound annual growth rate from the roughly $83,557 price the firm used as of September 30, 2026. Bitwise’s bear case is $130,686 and its bull case is $3.67 million.

The base case rests on three arguments. Institutional investors will keep adding bitcoin to portfolios. New supply stays fixed on a predictable schedule. Rising government debt will push investors toward assets that cannot be printed. 

Institutional investors love bitcoin

Bitwise estimates that institutions controlling about $147 trillion could allocate 1% to 5% of their portfolios to bitcoin, which the firm says would mean $1.5 trillion to $7.4 trillion of purchases. The network issues about $14 billion in new coins per year, and Bitwise argues that gap will push prices higher.

Institutional plumbing is already expanding. U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about $108 billion, according to the report. Banks and brokerages are building custody and trading services, and a recent report describes sovereign wealth funds and family offices buying during the 2026 decline. 

Regulators are also moving. A Federal Reserve capital proposal aimed at easing bank custody rules could widen access for large institutions, if adopted.

The past year tested that thesis. Bitcoin fell 53.4% from its October 2025 peak of $126,080 to a June 30, 2026 low of $58,717. Bitwise calls that drawdown the shallowest in the asset’s history. Prior cycle declines were 77%, 84% and 86%. 

Whether the shallow decline signals a new pattern or a pause is less settled. Bitwise expects the four-year cycle to weaken as the investor base broadens. Others see the cycle still at work. 

VanEck argues the current slump follows the historical halving pattern, and Fidelity has pointed to a possible floor around November 2026 if past timing holds. NYDIG has said a repeat of earlier bear markets could push the cycle low near $38,000 to $39,000. Cathie Wood has argued the market is nearly through the downturn. Each view carries a different price floor and timeline.

Bitcoin’s volatility 

Volatility is the other pillar of the forecast. Bitwise models a 27.8% average volatility over the decade, the midpoint between today’s level and its 2036 expectation. Grayscale’s research head recently put one-year volatility at 43%, against a 10-year average of 64%, and lower than the volatility of 19% of S&P 500 companies. Charles Schwab’s research found the asset remains prone to sharp drawdowns despite the lower readings. A Deutsche Bank analyst has described the trend as a sign of a maturing market.

Bitwise also reports that bitcoin’s correlation with gold reached a record 0.58 in September 2026. The firm expects that relationship to deepen, which positions bitcoin as a store-of-value asset. That link cuts both ways. If gold weakens, bitcoin may lose the support it gained from the same investor demand. Gemini has predicted that at least one country will shift part of its gold reserves into bitcoin in 2026, a forecast that has yet to materialize.

The report is candid about what could go wrong. Bitcoin’s track record is short. Its software was developed in 2008 and 2009, trading began on public exchanges in 2010, the first institutional product with bitcoin exposure launched in 2014, and spot ETPs arrived in 2024. 

Bitwise writes that forecasts built heavily on history carry uncertainty because future returns may differ from the past. Regulation is a second concern. The Clarity Act’s failure in Congress, which the report traces to Democratic concerns about ethics provisions, shows that progress can stall, even as the firm argues recent advances are unlikely to be rolled back. 

Technology is a third. Quantum computing, and mathematical advances accelerated by AI, could threaten the cryptography that secures bitcoin wallets. Bitwise says the network will need a major upgrade at some point, and holders who fail to move funds to new addresses could be exposed. The developers have made progress over the past year, the report says, but major issues remain unresolved.

Bitcoin’s price is near $80,500.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Zcash (ZEC) Price Prediction: Whale Goes Long Before FOMC Announcement as H&S Pattern Puts $1,350 in Focus
summary: Zcash (ZEC) is approaching a key resistance zone as a prominent crypto whale builds a multimillion-dollar leveraged long position ahead of the Federal Reserve’s October 28 interest rate decision.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ZEC

Zcash (ZEC) is approaching a key resistance zone as a prominent crypto whale builds a multimillion-dollar leveraged long position ahead of the Federal Reserve’s October 28 interest rate decision.

Traders are watching whether Zcash price can break above $1,350, potentially confirming a bullish chart pattern and opening the way toward higher targets.

ZEC recently traded around $1,280–$1,313 following a strong recovery. Improving technical indicators, rising adoption of bridged ZEC on Solana, and the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcement have brought renewed attention to the cryptocurrency.

Whale Opens $6.2 Million ZEC Long Before FOMC Announcement

A prominent crypto whale has reportedly opened a leveraged position worth approximately $79 million across Bitcoin (BTC) and Zcash. The exposure includes $72.5 million in BTC and $6.2 million in ZEC, with nearly $1 million in unrealized gains ahead of the Fed announcement.

A prominent crypto whale opened a $79 million leveraged long position in Bitcoin and Zcash, recording nearly $1 million in unrealized gains ahead of today’s FOMC meeting. Source: @cryptorover via X

The timing has drawn attention because interest rate expectations can influence demand for risk assets. A rate hold accompanied by a less restrictive policy outlook could support cryptocurrency prices, although the whale’s positioning does not guarantee a rally.

The Federal Reserve entered the October 28 meeting with its target federal funds rate at 3.75%–4.00%, following a 25-basis-point rate increase in September, according to the supplied market context. Investors are watching the policy statement and Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for signals about future rate decisions.

For ZEC, the immediate question is whether buying pressure can push the price through resistance. Leverage can amplify gains but also increase liquidation risks during sharp reversals, making the whale’s position a market signal rather than confirmation of a bullish trend.

ZEC Price Prediction: Inverse Head-and-Shoulders Pattern Puts $1,350 Resistance in Focus

An analysis shared by X user @MstrTranquility identifies a potential inverse head-and-shoulders pattern on ZEC’s daily chart, with a neckline near $1,350 and a projected target of $1,780 if a breakout is confirmed.

Zcash is forming a daily inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, with a breakout above the $1,350 neckline potentially targeting $1,780. Source: @MstrTranquility via X

The bullish formation typically consists of three troughs, with the middle trough forming the deepest low. A sustained move above the neckline can signal strengthening buying pressure, but a brief spike above resistance may not be enough to validate the pattern.

The analysis also emphasizes accepting failed setups objectively. If ZEC falls back below the neckline, the bullish formation may remain incomplete. Traders are therefore watching for a sustained close above $1,350 rather than relying on an intraday move.

Zcash Technical Analysis: Bullish Momentum Faces Key Resistance

ZEC’s technical indicators show improving momentum, although several resistance levels remain ahead. The supplied TradingView data places the daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) around 53–55, indicating moderate bullish momentum without reaching the commonly watched overbought threshold near 70.

Zcash (ZEC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The daily Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) histogram is positive, while price remains above many key moving averages. These signals support a constructive outlook but do not rule out a pullback after the recent recovery.

Immediate resistance sits around $1,317–$1,339, followed by $1,350–$1,364. A sustained daily close above the latter zone could bring $1,386 and $1,397 into focus, with further technical resistance near $1,470.

On the downside, $1,264 is a key near-term support. A daily close below this level could expose the $1,187–$1,200 area, followed by $1,058–$1,090.

Volatility remains elevated, with the supplied Average True Range (ATR) near $106–$113. This reinforces the need to account for potentially large price swings when managing positions and setting stop-loss levels.

Zcash Forms Another Descending Wedge on the Weekly Chart

A separate analysis by TradingView contributor VincePrince identifies a developing descending wedge on ZEC’s weekly chart. The analysis describes the token trading above a rising trendline that has supported previous pullbacks.

Zcash’s descending wedge breakout triggered a strong bullish rally from the ascending trendline, which remains a key technical support level. Source: VincePrince on TradingView

According to the contributor, an earlier descending wedge preceded a strong upward move, while a new formation could provide another breakout opportunity. A move above the upper trendline would be needed to strengthen this bullish scenario.

Descending wedges form as price swings narrow between downward-sloping trendlines. They are often viewed as bullish when price breaks above the formation, but confirmation depends on actual price action.

This weekly setup differs from the daily inverse head-and-shoulders pattern. Both suggest potential upside, but neither guarantees a rally. If ZEC clears $1,350 and holds the level during subsequent pullbacks, higher resistance zones could come into focus. Failure to break through could leave the token trading within its current range.

Zcash Adoption Grows as Bridged ZEC on Solana Hits Record

Zcash adoption is also expanding across blockchain networks. The amount of ZEC bridged to Solana reached approximately 103,000 tokens, valued at around $124 million, by late October. Most arrived through NEAR’s OmniBridge, according to the supplied reports.

Zcash bridged to Solana has reached a record 103,000 ZEC worth approximately $124 million, with most tokens transferred through NEAR’s OmniBridge. Source: @BSCNews via X

Holders of the OmniBridge version of ZEC increased from roughly 17,000 in late June to more than 152,000 by late October, representing nearly ninefold growth. The increase suggests broader participation in Solana’s trading ecosystem rather than activity driven solely by large holders.

Solana has become a significant venue for ZEC decentralized exchange trading. However, bridged ZEC does not automatically retain Zcash’s native privacy features. As an SPL token on Solana, its balances and transactions are publicly visible. Users must distinguish between this representation and shielded transactions on Zcash’s native network.

Growing bridged supply and holder numbers indicate increased participation, but they do not independently establish future price direction. Adoption metrics need to be assessed alongside liquidity, trading activity, and broader market conditions.

Zcash Price Outlook: FOMC Decision and $1,350 Breakout Remain Key

ZEC’s near-term direction depends on the Fed’s policy guidance, leveraged positioning, and its ability to overcome resistance. A less restrictive outlook could support risk assets, while persistent inflation concerns or signals of tighter policy could weigh on sentiment.

With the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00%, investors are focused on whether the Fed’s statement and press conference offer clues about future rate decisions. The outcome could influence crypto-market volatility, although its effect on ZEC will depend on how traders interpret the announcement.

A sustained breakout above $1,350 would strengthen the technical outlook, placing $1,386–$1,397 in focus. The inverse head-and-shoulders analysis identifies $1,780 as a potential target if the pattern confirms.

Conversely, rejection at resistance or a break below $1,264 would weaken the immediate bullish setup and expose lower support levels. For now, improving momentum and growing bridged-token participation support market interest, but the $1,350 resistance zone and the Fed’s guidance remain key factors in determining ZEC’s next move.

title: U.S. Treasury Says U.S. ‘Will Win in the Digital Asset Stack’ as Clarity Act Stalls
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Says U.S. ‘Will Win in the Digital Asset Stack’ as Clarity Act Stalls
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that U.S. leadership in digital assets could reinforce the dollar’s global reach even as the stalled CLARITY Act leaves regulators to fill the gap.
This post U....
content:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that American leadership in digital assets could reinforce the dollar’s global position, even as Congress has stalled on the market-structure legislation meant to govern them.

Speaking at Ripple’s Swell conference in New York with CEO Brad Garlinghouse, Bessent argued that the foundations of reserve-currency power are shifting. For much of modern history, he said, the dollar’s dominance rested largely on military strength. 

“We will keep our military umbrella, but increasingly, it becomes a technological umbrella,” he said. 

He grouped digital assets with artificial intelligence and semiconductors as areas where the United States and China are competing to build dominant infrastructure, and suggested the financial rails countries choose will shape the dollar’s reach.

The most concrete link he drew runs through stablecoins, dollar-pegged tokens whose issuers typically hold reserves that include U.S. Treasury securities. Bessent said stablecoins could give people in countries with high inflation or volatile currencies easier access to dollars. 

CoinGecko data puts the share of stablecoins denominated in dollars above 98%, with Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC the largest. Bessent himself put the figure above 90%. The exact number differs, but the dollar clearly dominates the category.

Bessent has also argued that stablecoin reserves could increase demand for Treasury debt. Last year he suggested stablecoins could generate $2 trillion in short-term demand for Treasuries and bills. That projection depends on how quickly stablecoin supply grows, what reserve rules apply, and how issuers choose to invest.

Bitcoin traded around $80,000 to $81,000 this week ahead of the Federal Reserve decision. Bitcoin advocates have long argued that a neutral, non-issuer asset offers something different from dollar-pegged tokens.

Broader crypto legislation trends

The regulatory backdrop is more uncertain. The Comptroller of the Currency has finalized its rule implementing the GENIUS Act, which sets requirements for payment stablecoin issuers. The federal framework takes effect January 18, 2027. 

The broader CLARITY Act, which would establish market-structure rules for digital assets, failed a Senate procedural vote on September 15, 49 to 50, short of the 60 votes needed. Disputes included ethics provisions related to federal officials’ crypto interests and stablecoin yield. 

Banks and the White House clashed over those yield terms.

Treasury Bessent’s willingness to work around Clarity Act failure

Bessent called the setback disappointing. He said Treasury could work with the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to address regulatory gaps. “At Treasury, we have a lot of convening powers,” he said, describing the agencies as “great partners.” 

He also said regulators could set guardrails to prevent banks from cutting off crypto firms, a practice known as debanking. 

“I think we can set up regulatory best practices, guardrails that will prevent that from happening again,” he said.

Those remarks did not set out a formal plan, working group, or timeline. Agency action can clarify rules within existing authority, but it lacks the permanence of an act of Congress, and it can be reversed by a future administration. 

Next week’s midterm elections could further stall the CLARITY Act, according to TD Cowen.

Micah Zimmerman

title: Brazilian Banking Giant Itaú Formalizes Crypto Role as Brazil Closes Its Licensing Window
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Brazilian Banking Giant Itaú Formalizes Crypto Role as Brazil Closes Its Licensing Window
Itaú has formally registered with Brazil’s central bank to intermediate and custody crypto assets under the new licensing rules.
This post Brazilian Banking Giant Itaú Formalizes Crypto Role a...
content:
Itaú Unibanco, the largest private bank in Brazil, has formalized its role as a cryptocurrency service provider before the Central Bank of Brazil. The filing covers intermediation and custody of crypto assets, the same activities the regulator assigns to brokerage firms, according to local reports. The news arrives as the country’s crypto sector faces a compressed timeline to obtain licenses.

Itaú’s move places the bank inside a licensing framework that did not exist a year ago. Brazil’s central bank requires every company that holds, moves, or trades crypto for customers to register as a regulated provider. By filing, Itaú tells the market that it intends to be one of them.

For Brazilian users, the change matters most for custody. A provider that holds crypto for clients must keep those assets separate from the firm’s own money, meet minimum capital requirements, and follow the same governance and anti-money laundering standards that apply to securities brokers. 

Clients of an authorized bank gain a clearer legal footing than clients of an unregulated app or an offshore exchange. For the bank, the filing is a commitment. A regulated crypto operation carries compliance costs, audit obligations, and reporting duties that smaller competitors may struggle to meet. 

The move also signals that Brazil’s biggest lenders plan to keep crypto inside the domestic financial system rather than leave it to foreign platforms.

Itau’s embrace of bitcoin and crypto

Itaú’s crypto story started before the new rules. The bank announced plans for crypto custody in 2022, when it was building a tokenization platform. In late 2025, it began letting retail clients buy and sell bitcoin through its investment app, íon. The crypto assets traded on íon are held in custody by Itaú itself, which made the bank’s position an operational one long before it became a regulatory one.

The regulatory backdrop came in 2025 and early 2026, when the central bank published Resolutions 519, 520, and 521. They created a new license category called Sociedades Prestadoras de Serviços de Ativos Virtuais, or SPSAVs, and the rules took effect February 2, 2026. 

The framework sorts providers into three categories: intermediaries, custodians, and brokers. It requires formal segregation of client and company assets, sets minimum capital levels, and extends the customer protection, governance, internal control, security, and anti-money laundering rules that already govern banks and brokers. 

Resolution 521 brought crypto transactions into the foreign-exchange regime. Transfers with unauthorized counterparties face a $100,000 cap, which limits how crypto moves across borders outside regulated channels.

Companies already operating when the regime took effect had to file for authorization within a transition period. 

That timing is why Itaú’s filing reads as a response to a pressure point, not a routine update.

Stricter standards follow. On July 1, 2026, the central bank approved tighter rules. Beginning in 2027, providers must meet financial security requirements similar to those for securities brokers and distributors. 

The regulator also barred institutions in Segment 5, the simplified-rules category for smaller banks, from offering virtual asset services. That decision pushes crypto activity toward larger, better-capitalized players, the group Itaú belongs to.

title: dxFeed Courts Indicator Sellers Days Before TradingView Closes Off-Platform Sales
summary:
Market data provider dxFeed pitched its dxScript scripting engine today (Wednesday) to firms that sell paid trading indicators. It tied the offer to new TradingView rules for invite-only scripts.
From Sunday, November 1, access to those scripts on TradingView can be sold only through its Marketplace...
content:
2026-10-28T15:24:02.754+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 13:24 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Its dxScript engine runs custom trading tools inside a firm’s own app, with an AI agent writing the code.
  • From Sunday, paid invite-only scripts can be sold only through the charting platform’s store.

Market data provider dxFeed pitched its dxScript scripting engine today (Wednesday) to firms that sell paid trading indicators. It tied the offer to new TradingView rules for invite-only scripts.

From Sunday, November 1, access to those scripts on TradingView can be sold only through its Marketplace, and vendors who keep taking payment elsewhere risk having their scripts blocked, as FinanceMagnates.com reported when TradingView moved paid indicator sales onto its own store.

That store listed 52 paid spaces today, priced from $4.99 to $199 a month, the same count as on Tuesday by FinanceMagnates.com's tally. TradingView said in August that more than 1,000 authors had applied for one.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Scripting Inside a Firm's Own App

dxFeed, a subsidiary of trading technology firm Devexperts, describes dxScript as a component that brokers, fintech firms and indicator sellers can add to a product they already run. Buyers keep their own branding and commercial model and do not need to build a scripting language, dxFeed said.

The engine launched in July as a JavaScript-based language running on dxFeed market data, with backtesting and signal alerts listed as later additions.

The name is older. Devexperts introduced DXscript in 2021 for traders writing their own indicators, and opened its DXcharts library to custom JavaScript indicators in March.

An AI agent built into dxScript turns trading logic written in plain language into code, according to dxFeed. TradingView took a different route in September, connecting its accounts to AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude for market data, screeners and alerts.

Denis Krivolapov, product manager for dxScript at dxFeed, said trading technology was moving toward a modular model in which firms add what they need without rebuilding their stack.

"Scripting should be one of those building blocks," he said.

What a Seller Gives Up in Each Store

Indicator sellers who stay inside a platform's store pay it a share of each sale, and the rates differ. MetaTrader and cTrader are among the platforms whose vendor web traffic FM Intelligence's platform comparison tool tracks by country.

TradingView's Creator Program terms put its platform fee at 0% with no end date, after an earlier version said the rate would apply at least until October 1, 2026, as FinanceMagnates.com noted when cTrader added subscriptions for paid tool creators in August.

MetaQuotes takes 20% of sales in its MQL5 Market, according to the store's rules, while Spotware keeps 30% in the cTrader Store it opened to algo developers in December 2024. That puts the cut across the three stores at 0% to 30% of each sale.

title: Bitcoin Price Today: BTC Outperforms S&P 500 Above $80K as Fed Interest Rate Decision Looms
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) climbed back above $80,500 on October 27, recovering from recent weakness as traders prepared for the Federal Reserve’s October 28 interest rate decision.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) climbed back above $80,500 on October 27, recovering from recent weakness as traders prepared for the Federal Reserve’s October 28 interest rate decision.

Bitcoin was hovering near $81,412 in the latest TradingView readings provided for October 28, keeping the $80,000 level in focus ahead of the policy announcement.

Prediction markets placed the probability of the Fed holding its benchmark interest rate steady at 94%, according to the latest market data. However, investors are also watching Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for clues about the policy outlook, particularly whether persistent inflation could lead to tighter monetary conditions later this year.

The latest recovery comes as Bitcoin shows signs of improving relative performance against the S&P 500. At the same time, on-chain analytics firm Glassnode has identified a shift toward net short positions among large Bitcoin traders on Hyperliquid, adding another source of uncertainty to the near-term Bitcoin price outlook.

Bitcoin Price Today: BTC Holds Above $80K Ahead of Fed Decision

Bitcoin’s return above $80,000 puts the market near a closely watched price zone ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee’s announcement. The latest BTC price readings place the cryptocurrency around $81,412, with trading activity concentrated near several short-term technical indicators and pivot levels.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Federal Reserve’s current target range for the federal funds rate is 3.75% to 4.00%, following its September rate increase. Markets broadly expect policymakers to leave rates unchanged at this meeting, although the accompanying statement and Warsh’s comments could influence expectations for the next policy move.

The decision is scheduled for 2 p.m. Eastern Time on October 28, followed by the Fed chair’s press conference. The distinction between the rate decision and the subsequent guidance matters for Bitcoin because an expected hold may already be reflected in prices, leaving traders focused on any unexpected change in the Fed’s assessment of inflation and economic conditions.

Markets expect the Fed to hold rates at 3.75%–4.00%, while dovish signals could trigger Bitcoin short liquidations toward $88,000. Source: @bitgu_ru via X

Crypto trader @bitgu_ru outlined several possible outcomes tied to the tone of the announcement. In that analysis, dovish comments could support a move toward $88,000, while a more hawkish message could expose BTC to a decline toward $75,900–$78,200. An unexpected rate increase was presented as a more severe downside scenario, with $67,900 identified as a potential target.

These levels represent scenarios from the trader’s analysis rather than confirmed market forecasts. The eventual reaction will depend on how the Fed’s decision compares with expectations, alongside liquidity conditions, positioning, and broader financial-market sentiment.

Bitcoin Outperforms the S&P 500 as Session Win Rate Improves

Glassnode reported that Bitcoin has regained an edge over the S&P 500 in recent trading sessions. Its analysis showed BTC’s daily session win rate moving above 50% on October 20, meaning Bitcoin recorded more winning sessions than losing ones over the period being tracked.

Bitcoin regained its edge over the S&P 500, with its daily win rate surpassing 50% on October 20, 2026. Source: Glassnode via X

The shift follows a difficult stretch in June 2026, when Bitcoin won only one of every five sessions, its weakest result in more than five years, according to the supplied Glassnode findings. The recent improvement suggests that Bitcoin’s relative performance has strengthened after a prolonged period of underperformance.

A session win rate measures how frequently an asset records a positive session under a defined methodology. It does not necessarily mean Bitcoin has delivered a higher total return than the S&P 500 over every period, nor does it establish that the trend will continue. The broader indexed-price comparison and excess returns per session provide additional context for assessing the change.

Glassnode’s analysis also points to the possibility that sustained outperformance could attract further capital. Investors sometimes increase exposure to assets that have recently performed better, potentially reinforcing an existing trend. However, this type of flow can reverse quickly if market conditions deteriorate or the asset loses its relative advantage.

For the current Bitcoin price outlook, the comparison with equities offers a useful measure of market strength. Bitcoin’s improving session record provides a constructive signal, but the upcoming Fed announcement could test whether that relative performance can persist through a fresh macroeconomic catalyst.

Hyperliquid Whales Turn Net Short as BTC Trades Near $80K

Despite Bitcoin’s recovery, positioning among large traders has become more cautious. Glassnode reported that tracked whales on Hyperliquid shifted to net short Bitcoin perpetual futures last week for the first time since March 2026.

Hyperliquid whales turned net short on Bitcoin perpetuals for the first time since March 2026, after correctly anticipating the recent price bottom. Source: Glassnode via X

Net short positioning means that short exposure exceeds long exposure within the group being measured. Traders may establish such positions to profit from a decline, hedge existing holdings, or manage exposure to volatility. The data therefore indicates a change in positioning, not a guarantee that the market will fall.

The shift is notable because these traders had previously moved into long positions near Bitcoin’s recent price bottom. Their reversal as BTC returned to the $80,000 area suggests that some large participants are preparing for additional downside or are reducing their confidence in an immediate recovery.

Glassnode’s findings leave two broad possibilities. If Bitcoin breaks below important support levels, the increase in bearish positioning could accompany a deeper correction. If BTC instead rebounds toward $85,000, traders holding short positions could face pressure to close them, potentially adding buying demand to the move.

A short squeeze occurs when rising prices force short sellers to buy back positions to limit losses or meet margin requirements. Such buying can accelerate an advance, particularly when leverage is elevated. However, the scale of any squeeze would depend on the size and concentration of positions, available liquidity, and the speed of the price move.

For now, the change in whale positioning creates a counterweight to Bitcoin’s improving performance against equities. The Fed’s decision may provide a catalyst, but price action around support and resistance will be important in determining whether traders’ defensive positioning proves timely.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: Technical Indicators Show a Neutral Bias

TradingView’s technical summary for BTCUSD on Bitstamp showed a broadly neutral picture in the latest readings supplied for October 28. Across the combined set of oscillators and moving averages, the summary recorded nine sell signals, nine neutral readings, and eight buy signals.

Oscillators were also predominantly neutral, with two sell readings, eight neutral readings, and one buy reading. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stood at 48, indicating neither an overbought nor an oversold condition. The Average Directional Index (ADX) was at 17, suggesting that the prevailing trend lacked strong directional momentum under the indicator’s usual interpretation.

Other momentum measures leaned slightly bearish. The Momentum (10) indicator registered a sell signal, while the MACD level was also negative and rated sell. These readings were offset by a buy signal from Bull Bear Power and a more balanced set of moving-average signals.

The moving averages show why the immediate bitcoin price prediction remains uncertain. BTC was trading above several longer-term averages, including the 100-period and 200-period exponential moving averages at approximately $77,766 and $76,396, respectively. The 100-period and 200-period simple moving averages were also below the current price, at roughly $75,924 and $73,067.

By contrast, several intermediate averages remained above the latest price. The 20-period exponential moving average stood near $81,717, while the 20-period simple moving average was around $81,842. The 30-period simple moving average was higher still, near $82,697. This split indicates that longer-term trend measures remain comparatively supportive while shorter-term indicators reflect the recent pullback.

BTC Price Levels to Watch

The TradingView pivot calculations identify the $81,950 area as the central classic pivot, with the Ichimoku base line near $83,057. Together, these levels create an initial resistance zone that Bitcoin would need to clear to strengthen its short-term recovery.

Above that area, the Camarilla resistance levels stand near $84,705, $85,847, and $86,989. These levels overlap with the broader $85,000–$87,500 supply zone highlighted in Glassnode’s October market analysis, where selling interest and liquidation clusters have been concentrated. A sustained move through this region would provide stronger evidence that buyers are absorbing overhead supply.

BTC bounced off the bottom of the descending channel and is back at the level that capped it. Source: CryptoCT01 on TradingView

The $80,000 level remains an important reference point. The Camarilla support levels are near $81,278 and $80,136, while the classic S1 pivot sits at $76,526. Fibonacci pivot support is near $77,190, with additional levels lower down. These are technical reference points rather than guaranteed turning points.

  • Bullish scenario: If BTC holds above $80,000 and moves decisively through the $81,950–$83,057 resistance zone, traders may monitor $84,700–$85,000 as the next test. A sustained break above that area could bring the $85,000–$87,500 supply zone into focus, with $88,000 representing a further upside scenario from the trader analysis. Stronger confirmation would require sustained price acceptance above resistance rather than a brief intraday spike.
  • Bearish scenario: A failure to hold $80,000 would weaken the near-term structure and put the mid-to-high $70,000s into focus. The $78,200–$75,900 region overlaps with downside levels identified in the supplied FOMC scenario analysis and several technical support references. A deeper decline toward $67,900 would require a more substantial deterioration in market conditions and should not be treated as the base case solely because it appears in a trader’s scenario.

These levels are based on the supplied TradingView snapshot and market analysis. Indicator values can change as new candles form, while pivot levels depend on the underlying calculation period. Traders should confirm the readings against live charts before using them to assess risk.

Fed Guidance Could Set the Next Direction for Bitcoin

The October 28 FOMC decision places monetary policy at the center of the near-term Bitcoin outlook. A rate hold that matches expectations may have a limited immediate effect if markets have already priced it in. The more consequential signal could come from Warsh’s comments about inflation, the economic outlook, and the possibility of another rate increase.

A dovish tone could improve risk appetite by reducing concerns about tighter financial conditions. Such a reaction may support Bitcoin and other risk-sensitive assets, although the response would also depend on Treasury yields, the US dollar, and broader equity-market performance.

A hawkish message could have the opposite effect. If policymakers emphasize persistent inflation or signal that further tightening remains possible, traders may reassess the outlook for liquidity and risk assets. Bitcoin could then face renewed selling pressure, especially if bearish derivatives positioning coincides with a break below support.

The wider market backdrop remains important. Bitcoin’s improved session win rate against the S&P 500 offers evidence of a relative recovery, but the shift in Hyperliquid whale positioning shows that large derivatives traders are not uniformly confident in further gains. The two signals measure different aspects of the market and can coexist.

For investors tracking Bitcoin price news today, the key indicators are therefore the Fed’s policy language, BTC’s ability to defend $80,000, and its reaction around the $82,000–$83,000 resistance area. A sustained breakout could strengthen the recovery case, while a decisive support failure would increase the risk of a deeper pullback.

Bitcoin has recovered above $80,000, but the technical indicators remain mixed and large-trader positioning has turned more defensive. The Fed’s decision and subsequent press conference may help determine which signal gains the upper hand. Until price breaks clearly beyond the current trading range, a neutral outlook remains consistent with the available evidence.

summary: Cardano (ADA) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as bulls defend key support levels while traders weigh the chances of a bullish recovery or further downside.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ADA

Cardano (ADA) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as bulls defend key support levels while traders weigh the chances of a bullish recovery or further downside.

Cardano price is trading close to an important support area after another volatile stretch, with price action now beginning to attract stronger attention from larger holders. According to Brave New Coin, ADA is trading around $0.20, down 2.64% over the past 24 hours.

Cardano Approaches $0.197-$0.213 Support Zone

Cardano is moving into an area where the next meaningful reaction could begin. The four-hour chart shared by Crypto Crown places immediate support around $0.197, with the broader reaction zone extending toward roughly $0.213. Price is currently trading close to the lower end of that region after several weeks of declining momentum.

Cardano is approaching a key reaction area around $0.197-$0.213, with $0.2356 and $0.2592 marking the next important upside levels if support holds. Source: Crypto Crown via X.

The ADA chart also highlights liquidity around $0.189, which makes the lower part of the range particularly important. A brief sweep into that area followed by a recovery would still fit the bullish scenario. If buyers can establish a base here, $0.213 becomes the first level to recover, followed by approximately $0.2356. The larger resistance sits near $0.2592, which would become increasingly relevant if Cardano starts producing higher lows from the current zone.

ADA Whale Activity Picks Up Near $0.20

The timing is positive for bulls because the surge in whale activity is arriving while ADA is still trading near support rather than after a major breakout. Large transactions picked up as price moved from around $0.21 towards $0.23, suggesting bigger players are becoming more active as Cardano tries to build a base.

If that activity continues while ADA holds around $0.20, it would strengthen the idea that larger holders are positioning ahead of a recovery rather than simply reacting to strength. That would give bulls a better foundation for another push toward the higher resistance zones.

ADA whale transactions above $1 million have risen sharply. Source: Santiment data via Ali Charts on X.

Cardano Ascending Channel Keeps $0.30-$0.36 in View

Cardano is still holding inside the broader ascending structure that has shaped the recovery from its earlier lows. The latest pullback has brought ADA price back toward the lower part of that channel, but price has not yet broken the sequence of higher lows that has supported the move so far.

The immediate question is whether ADA price can recover the mid-$0.20s and start pushing back through nearby resistance. A sustained move above that area would improve the structure and bring $0.30 into focus, while continued strength would leave the upper part of the channel around $0.35-$0.36 as the next larger area to watch.

The technical setup is also being supported by activity around the Cardano ecosystem. The Money Ape points to Pump.fun bringing roughly 17 million monthly active traders into the broader environment, while Charles Hoskinson continues working on privacy-focused transaction infrastructure. Those developments do not determine the next price move on their own, but they give the recovery a stronger backdrop if buyers can keep the channel intact.

Source: The Money Ape via X

For now, the structure remains strong above the lower channel boundary. A break through the mid-$0.20s would provide stronger confirmation that the rebound is developing into something more sustainable, while failure to hold the channel would weaken the path toward the higher targets.

Contrary View: Zig-zag Structure Could Drag ADA to $0.150

Cardano may still have more volatility to work through before the broader recovery becomes cleaner. Kevin Mercer’s chart maps out a zig-zag structure in which ADA continues to alternate between sharp rebounds and deeper pullbacks rather than moving higher in a straight line.

The chart places the current price near $0.217, with the projected corrective path extending toward roughly $0.15-$0.145 before a stronger recovery phase develops. That makes the $0.20-$0.19 region an important intermediate area to watch, as a failure to stabilize there would keep the lower target in play.

Cardano’s broader structure may continue producing sharp swings in both directions before a cleaner trend develops. Source: Kevin Mercer via X.

The broader recovery case therefore does not necessarily depend on ADA rallying immediately from current levels. If price eventually establishes a base around the $0.15 area, the projected structure leaves room for a much stronger rebound toward roughly $0.25-$0.27 during the next expansion phase.

For now, Mercer’s view keeps expectations measured: ADA could remain volatile through the corrective leg, but a successful base around $0.145-$0.150 would preserve the possibility of a larger recovery toward the mid-$0.20s.

Cardano Moving Averages Under Pressure

Cardano remains below its main short-term moving averages, leaving the 12-hour structure tilted bearish despite the latest attempt to stabilize near $0.20. The chart shows the 5-period average around $0.2130, the 20-period near $0.2136, the 25-period around $0.2152, and the 30-period near $0.2177.

That alignment keeps overhead pressure in place because price is trading beneath the full cluster rather than reclaiming it. The averages are still sloping lower, suggesting the broader short-term trend has not yet turned, even though selling momentum has started to cool.

A recovery through roughly $0.213-$0.218 would be the first sign that ADA is beginning to regain control of the trend. Until then, the moving averages continue to act as dynamic resistance, with price needing to move back above the cluster before the recovery can look more convincing.

Final Outlook: Can Cardano Price Prediction Rally in Q4?

Cardano price enters the next stage of Q4 with a more interesting setup than price alone suggests. Whale activity is rising, the broader ascending structure remains intact, and several technical views still leave room for a larger recovery if buyers can continue defending the current region.

For the broader outlook, the next recovery through the mid-$0.20s would begin bringing the larger Cardano Price Prediction targets back into focus. A sustained move higher could reopen $0.30 first, followed by the $0.35-$0.36 region, while continued weakness would keep ADA in a corrective phase for longer.

title: Gold Price Analysis October 2026 as Fed Decision Puts Key Support at Risk
summary: The top-of-the-queue decision from the Fed on Oct. 28 will be the main trigger, and interest-rate expectations will likely be a factor in the dollar, Treasuries, and precious-metal demand.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

The top-of-the-queue decision from the Fed on Oct. 28 will be the main trigger, and interest-rate expectations will likely be a factor in the dollar, Treasuries, and precious-metal demand.

Gold is getting close to a technical crossroads in November. XAU/USD has suffered a significant pause from its record-high gains this year and is currently at a support level, which may be its next target.At press time, gold traded at $4,019.805, above the $3,978.180 low and 0.60% higher on the candle displayed. With this in mind, the $4,000 psychological level is now at the center of the current battle. But a modest recovery this week is no indication sellers have taken control.

Analyst Trading Identifies a Critical Support Test

Meanwhile, the analyst at Cheds Trading pronounces gold to be “right on the cusp of” support in the X post.

Bollinger Bands also expand when the price declines, indicating greater price volatility during the sell-off period.

The chart below displays price moving towards an obvious horizontal price support level and down from each higher high. Source: Cheds Via X

This structure is important since it is being tested after a prolonged period of downtrend. If the buyers do not back off from the low blue zone, then gold may try to come back in a relief move. If it breaks below, the chart indicates that the previous support area could also serve as resistance when the market recovers.

October’s Pullback Puts $4,000 in Focus

Notably, there are now three levels for a practical framework. First, $3,978 is the latest weekly low and the immediate downside reference. Second, the $4000 is a psychological barrier that buyers must overcome. Thirdly, $4,030 is the new candle high and the first hurdle to recover.

The most recent candle has been between $3,978.180 and $4,030.065, and, in the most recent correction, gold has been nudging closer to $4,000. Source: TradingView

The chart also shows some steep gains between 2024 and 2025 and then a significantly faster move in 2026.

If the price breaks above $4,030, it would indicate short-term buying, but in itself it would not prove a trend reversal. If $3,978 is broken, the bull market narrative may be weakened, and the price of gold could continue to fall. The liquidity heatmap on the chart indicates historical price levels, but they are not price levels that can be confirmed.

October 28 Fed Decision Is the Main Catalyst

Meanwhile, the FOMC will hold its next meeting on Oct. 27-28 and make its policy decision on Oct. 28. Investors can check the timing on the official calendar set up by the Federal Reserve.

Market sources indicate the move is being watched not only by the market but also for guidance at the next meeting. A hawkish message could strengthen the dollar and push up Treasury yields, raising the opportunity cost of holding gold. That would drive up the price of gold and silver futures if investors curb holdings of non-yielding investments.

Often, a more benign view would fuel an underperformance of the dollar and yields, possibly aiding precious metals. Financial conditions may also be getting easier for bitcoin, but crypto prices are still sensitive to positioning and overall risk appetite. Lithium futures and contracts could react to growth shifts but will also be influenced by battery demand and inventories and supplies.

What Investors Should Watch Before November

The first question is whether gold can sustain this 3,978–4,000 range as the Fed announcement comes. A bounce from $4,030 would support near-term bulls, but a significant move below the recent low would boost the prospects for more weakness. Investors also should keep an eye on the dollar and Treasury yields for further confirmation and not use the Fed announcement as a signal to buy or sell.

Any weekly price action below $3,978 would be a null setter of the prevailing interpretation of gold holding support, especially with a hawkish Fed signal and the dollar and Treasury yields rising.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What is significant about the Fed decision on October 28 for gold?

It has the potential to alter expectations with respect to future interest rates and impact the dollar, Treasury yields, and demand for non-yielding assets.

2. What is the most important level for gold now?

The weekly chart presented here focuses attention on 3,978-4,000, the current shown low, and the psychological $4,000.

3. What does Cheds Trading’s chart suggest?

Notice the shared chart with a downtrend of highs and a price test around a significant support level. A breakdown would impact the bullish support argument; a hold may mean that a recovery is possible.

4. Will a milder Fed performance be good for Bitcoin and silver?

Potentially. As lower rates and yields continue to be expected, precious metals and risk appetite should be supported, but there is no guarantee that either asset will rise.

5. What would indicate even more weakness in gold?

If the weekly chart closes below $3,978, the current support interpretation could be considered invalid. Without a break, it is impossible to set a price range for the price movement.
