title: ThinkMarkets and Pepperstone Open Bets on Anthropic’s Debut, Priced Two Different Ways
summary:
ThinkMarkets said today (Wednesday) it started quoting 24/7 contracts on Anthropic's and OpenAI's value at the close of their first trading day. Clients can go long or short, but the contracts are cash-settled CFDs that carry no shares and no IPO allocation.
Anthropic, whose Claude model powered nin...
content:
2026-10-28T11:48:38.794+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 09:48 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • One quotes first-day market value in billions, the other the expected opening share price, near $115.
  • The Claude developer filed for a Nasdaq listing on Monday as crypto futures put its value near $1.9 trillion.

ThinkMarkets said today (Wednesday) it started quoting 24/7 contracts on Anthropic's and OpenAI's value at the close of their first trading day. Clients can go long or short, but the contracts are cash-settled CFDs that carry no shares and no IPO allocation.

Anthropic, whose Claude model powered nine of 10 broker AI agents trading live accounts in the first half, filed for an IPO on Monday and applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.

Its registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC ) leaves the price range blank.

Crypto traders have already put a number on it. Perpetual futures tied to the listing implied a value of about $1.87 trillion on Binance on October 25 and 26, Bitcoin.com reported, almost double the $965 billion post-money valuation from Anthropic's May funding round.

London's trading industry is coming home!

OpenAI has said it will not go public this year and was last valued at $852 billion in a round that closed on March 31. It has also said tokens sold by Robinhood in Europe were not OpenAI equity.

Crypto Venues Quoted Anthropic Months Earlier

ThinkMarkets arrives four months or more after crypto exchanges and two smaller CFD brokers started selling the same exposure. Bitget opened an Anthropic perpetual in early June with leverage of up to 20 times.

OKX said on May 6 it would list perpetual futures on OpenAI, SpaceX and Anthropic, and later offered them to European clients, where the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) treats perpetual futures as CFDs subject to retail leverage caps.

On Hyperliquid, Ventuals ran OpenAI and Anthropic markets until June 15, when it wound down after more than $650 million in volume, CoinDesk reported. STARTRADER began offering OpenAI and Anthropic CFDs on June 29 with 5x leverage, and PU Prime listed the same two names around then.

Retail brokers ran the same race before SpaceX listed in June, when CMC Markets opened a grey market on the day Binance listed its pre-IPO perpetual in May. By FinanceMagnates.com's count, at least six venues quoted Anthropic before ThinkMarkets did.

Market Value or Share Price

Each ThinkMarkets contract tracks the company's expected market capitalization at the close of its first trading day, with one point worth $1 billion. A quote of 1,500 stands for a $1.5 trillion company.

Nauman Anees, co-founder and chief executive of ThinkMarkets, pointed to the trading hours as the reason for the launch.

"News on these listings does not wait for an exchange to open," he said.

Positions can be closed at any time while the market is quoted. Those held into the listing settle against the actual first-day closing value and do not turn into shares, the same split between owning stock and betting on its price that ran through the SpaceX debut.

Pepperstone, which extended its perpetual CFDs beyond SpaceX to metals, indices and oil in July, launched its own Anthropic market this week and quotes a different number.

Its perpetual CFD tracks the price traders expect Anthropic's shares to open at, around $115 on Wednesday, with pricing drawn from centralized and decentralized exchanges. Positions can roll into a contract on the listed shares after the debut, Pepperstone said.

Chris Weston, Pepperstone's head of research, said the market gives "a live read on investor sentiment as Anthropic moves towards its listing."

The crypto venues behind those prices hold a small book. Open Anthropic contracts across more than a dozen of them were worth $134 million, Forbes reported on Tuesday, citing data provider DeFiLlama.

Part of a Weekend Product Range

The new markets join ThinkMarkets' 24/7 gold, silver, oil and US index CFDs. Gold is the crowded part of that business: at least 19 firms launched a dedicated weekend or 24/7 gold product between February 17 and October 1, FM Intelligence data show.

ThinkMarkets accounted for about 0.4% of the retail FX and CFD volume tracked in FM Intelligence's Broker Volumes over the first half of 2026, up 12% from a year earlier.

title: Key Security Features Players Look For in Crypto Gaming Platforms
summary:
As crypto-based gaming grows, players expect security features that go beyond branding flair or promotional offers. Evaluating platform safeguards upfront is essential, especially when dealing with digital currencies and on-chain
The post Key Security Features Players Look For in Crypto Gaming Platf...
content:
As crypto-based gaming grows, players expect security features that go beyond branding flair or promotional offers. Evaluating platform safeguards upfront is essential, especially when dealing with digital currencies and on-chain transactions.

For anyone navigating crypto gaming, security is essential. Unlike traditional online gaming, crypto platforms process fast, irreversible transactions and often support self-custody. This raises the stakes for player protection and operational transparency. Even when incentives such as a No Deposit Bonus are available to attract users, player trust is ultimately dependent on strong technical and procedural safeguards, not simply on promotions.

  • Encryption, session management, and password standards
  • Account protections and anti-takeover measures
  • Wallet management and operational security
  • Fairness, transparency, and incident handling
  • Privacy, compliance, and warning signs
  • Checklist for evaluating security before depositing funds

Encryption, session management, and password standards

Players should expect modern crypto digital entertainment hubs to use end-to-end encryption for both data in transit and at rest. Platforms relying on TLS help keep traffic between browsers and servers confidential. Additional encryption of stored information protects accounts if systems are breached.

Protection extends beyond encryption. Platforms that support strong passwords and integrate with password managers help lower the risk of account compromise. Secure session handling, such as expiring inactive logins, further limits the impact of stolen credentials.

Account protections and anti-takeover measures

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is often available on reputable platforms. Whether through an authenticator app or a hardware key, it makes unauthorized access more difficult. Reliable platforms also provide clear recovery processes and notify you if your account is used on a new device.

Features like device management, withdrawal confirmations, and anti-phishing codes can help players quickly spot suspicious activity or attempts to redirect funds.

Wallet management and operational security

Understanding where and how your funds are stored is important. Platforms that keep most customer funds in cold storage (offline wallets) can lower hacking risk compared to storing large balances in hot wallets. Withdrawal controls such as whitelisting trusted addresses provide additional protection.

Clear operational security practices, like multi-signature authorization for large withdrawals, may indicate stronger internal controls.

Fairness, transparency, and incident handling

Digital gaming platforms sometimes offer provably fair systems, allowing you to verify random game results on-chain or through published algorithms. While this increases transparency, be aware that these systems generally cover only game fairness, not broader operational trust or overall randomness.

Certain platforms undergo independent audits of their random number generators and publish summaries. Transparent communication about security incidents, visible bug bounty programs, and regular patch management are signs of a commitment to operational trust.

Privacy, compliance, and warning signs

Minimizing data collection is considered best practice. Where verification is needed, secure and transparent handling of personal information is important. Watch for privacy policy gaps or unexpected requests for personal documents, as these might signal insufficient security measures.

Warning signs include vague security explanations, no visible audit history, or unclear incident communication. A sensible, user-friendly interface with easy-to-find security controls can indicate that user safety is a real priority.

Checklist for evaluating security before depositing funds

  • Verify that end-to-end encryption is active in your browser (look for HTTPS and certificate details).
  • Check for 2FA support and see if device session management is provided.
  • Review wallet custody practices and prefer platforms that use cold storage for user funds.
  • Look for references to independent RNG audits and transparent reporting of provably fair mechanisms.
  • Read the privacy policy and avoid platforms that request unnecessary personal data.
  • Evaluate how security incidents and updates are communicated to users.

title: GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty for Hackers as Japanese Brokers Tighten Logins
summary:
GMO Internet Group offered up to $1 million for information that leads to the identification and arrest of the hackers who breached its trading server service. The site where the attackers had posted customer data went offline early today (Wednesday).
The attackers began publishing what they said wa...
content:
2026-10-28T11:11:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 09:11 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The attackers’ leak site went offline overnight, and the bill for customer payouts cannot yet be calculated.
  • FXTF will lock out clients without two-step login from Saturday, while Dukascopy Japan reset passwords.

GMO Internet Group offered up to $1 million for information that leads to the identification and arrest of the hackers who breached its trading server service. The site where the attackers had posted customer data went offline early today (Wednesday).

The attackers began publishing what they said was customer data on Tuesday, after GMO refused a demand of about ¥8 billion (about $50 million). GMO said the domain was suspended at about 4:00 local time after it worked with other companies, and that it would move to take down any copies.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Brokers hit by the breach are now tightening logins for every client, not only those who rented GMO's servers. FXTF, which runs more than 280,000 accounts out of Tokyo, will lock clients out of its portal and platform from Saturday unless they switch on two-step login.

Brokers Make Two-Step Login Compulsory

FXTF already required one-time passwords on MT4 and MT5 . Today's notice extends the rule to its client portal and FXTF GX platform after weekly maintenance on October 31, and removes the option to close the setup window.

Codes go to the registered email address, so clients whose inbox cannot receive them will be shut out. FXTF, one of five brokers that confirmed unauthorized trades by Monday, becomes GW Securities on November 1.

Dukascopy Japan said today that some of its clients who used the GMO service had trades placed without consent. It changed passwords on accounts with suspected unauthorized logins and ended every open session, adding that it had found no sign its own systems were accessed.

OANDA Japan told clients on Tuesday that it is strengthening MT5 login security and asked those on rented servers to change the default remote desktop port and restrict which IP addresses can connect. OANDA plans to switch off MT4 on November 27.

XTB took the same step in Poland last year. It made two-step login compulsory for all clients hours after a customer said hackers had drained his account through rapid trades in thinly traded stocks.

GMO Says Costs Cannot Yet Be Calculated

In a filing to the Tokyo Stock Exchange today, GMO listed six kinds of payment linked to the breach. They include ¥5,000 for every user of the service, repayment of realized losses from unauthorized trades and a new PC for any customer hit by ransomware.

Customers whose data GMO confirms was published will get ¥10,000 to ¥25,000 for each category of information exposed, up to ¥3 million per disclosure. GMO said the total cannot be calculated until it knows how many customers qualify and what the published data covers.

GMO Internet Group is funding the bounty itself and began taking tips at noon. It said it "will never comply with the attacker's demands" and is working with the police.

GMO Internet Group shares closed 5.2% higher than on Tuesday at ¥3,324, after a 15.7% fall on Monday. GMO has not said how many customers had data published. Up to 26,739 servers may have been exposed, it said last week.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has asked her cabinet for emergency measures against cyberattacks by the end of next week, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

Account takeovers at online brokers were already a policy issue: fraudulent trades on hijacked accounts exceeded ¥500 billion between March and May 2025.

title: Arc Surges $1 Billion in USDC Circulating Supply
summary:

The post Arc Surges $1 Billion in USDC Circulating Supply appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Circle’s Arc blockchain has amassed over $1 billion worth of USDC about 6 weeks after its launch.
  • Arc’s stablecoin balance grew by 32% in the past week.
  • Extended reportedly transferred $120 million in trading collateral with the same 73% of the reported USDC supply transferred by four addresses.

Circle’s Arc is gaining rapid momentum and has garnered attention in the crypto industry due to its stablecoin portfolio. However, the number of addresses that own the majority of the funds suggest limited distribution of the liquidity across the network.

  • Arc’s USDC Holdings Surpass $1 Billion
  • Four Addresses Control 73% of the Reported Supply
  • Extended’s $120 Million Transfer Adds to Arc’s Growth

Arc’s USDC Holdings Surpass $1 Billion

Circle’s Arc blockchain has now surpassed the $1 billion milestone in terms of USDC holdings, just about six weeks since the chain’s launch. Over the past week, the capitalization of Arc’s stablecoins has increased by 32%.

USDC, a dollar-pegged stablecoin by Circle, plays a crucial role in the network’s operations. It’s there to give an idea of the dollar-denominated liquidity on Arc, so fluctuations in its supply are a key indicator of the early development of the blockchain.

However, there are some possibilities of high dollar transactions that can also add capital to a blockchain, and that results in a spike in the reported number of holdings, but without an equal number of people using the blockchain.

Read More: Circle Agent Marketplace Brings USDC Payments and Live Data Tools to Arc Blockchain

Four Addresses Control 73% of the Reported Supply

While Arc is growing quickly, the amount of USDC held seems to be concentrated in its hands. It is estimated that approximately 73% of all USDC is being held on these four addresses.

This focus means that a small subset of addresses could have a significant impact on Arc’s overall stablecoin reserves. Any significant deposits or withdrawals from these wallets could greatly alter the liquidity on the network.

Yet, wallet concentration does not mean that the funds actually belong to whom. The addresses might pertain to trading exchanges, liquidity suppliers, custodians, or others who are holding assets for a number of users.

Extended’s $120 Million Transfer Adds to Arc’s Growth

One reported transaction provides further context for Arc’s expanding balance. Extended, a perpetuals trading platform, reportedly transferred approximately $120 million in trading collateral from Starknet to Arc.

The movement highlights the importance of the actions of each crypto platform on a blockchain’s stablecoin reserves. However, the move could help bolster Arc’s position, not necessarily the overall amount of crypto investment.

The reported transaction also partly accounts for the reason that Arc’s weekly growth needs to be analyzed in conjunction with the activity of heavy balances. While 32% is significant, it is not sufficient to consider it as an indication of the establishment of liquidity on the network, as it does not necessarily account for the rest of the shares.

title: Adyen Scraps Its 2028 Margin Target and Cuts This Year’s to 50%
summary:

Merchant demand for the combined offer came in stronger than planned, the Dutch payments compan...
content:
2026-10-28T11:06:37.256+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 09:06 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The payments company will spend more on two acquisitions after merchant demand beat its plans.
  • Third-quarter net revenue rose 23% to €738.1 million, yet the shares fell as much as 13% in Amsterdam.

Adyen cut its 2026 profit margin forecast to 50% today (Wednesday) and dropped its target of a margin above 55% by 2028. It will spend more on Talon.One and Orb, two loyalty and billing firms it acquired.

Merchant demand for the combined offer came in stronger than planned, the Dutch payments company said.

The forecast is three percentage points below Adyen's 2025 EBITDA margin of 53%, and two below the roughly 52% implied in August, when it said the two deals would trim about one point from this year's margin.

Investors now have no profit target beyond 2026 until February, when Adyen will publish its 2027 objectives. The shares fell as much as 13% in early Amsterdam trading and were down about 11% at €837.10 by 9:42 a.m. CET, against €944.00 at Tuesday's close.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The margin cut came with a quarter that beat revenue forecasts. Net revenue rose 23% year over year to €738.1 million in the three months to September 30, or 22% at constant currency.

Analysts had expected €730.3 million, according to a company-compiled consensus cited by Reuters. Processed volume rose 30% to €451.1 billion.

Adyen's Margin Guidance Has Fallen Twice This Year

Measured by EBITDA margin, the profit benchmark Adyen guides on, the outlook has moved down at each update in 2026 and now matches a slower-growing European rival.

In February Adyen expected the 2026 margin to stay broadly in line with 2025 and to pass 55% by 2028. In August it reported a first-half margin of 49%, or 50% excluding acquisition costs, and kept the 2028 goal.

That leaves Adyen planning on the margin Nexi already runs at. The Italian processor reported a first-half EBITDA margin of 50.1% while its merchant revenue slipped 0.8%. Adyen is growing net revenue 23% for roughly the same margin.

Outlook Changes Have Moved the Stock Before

Wednesday's drop is smaller than two earlier sell-offs over growth or guidance. The shares fell nearly 39% in one day in August 2023, after first-half results showed slower growth.

They lost more than 20% shortly after the open in February this year, when Adyen guided for a flat 2026 margin, MarketScreener reported.

Spending Follows Two July Acquisitions

Adyen said merchant interest in combining payments with loyalty, billing and financial products had been stronger and broader than it expected, so it is accelerating planned investment in the Talon.One and Orb teams.

Co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage said the company sees "a significant opportunity ahead" and is "accelerating our investments across the business to capture it in full."

The two companies brought 399 employees with them, taking Adyen to 5,596 full-time staff at the end of September. It now plans to add 1,000 to 1,100 net new employees in 2026 including the deals, while its underlying hiring target of 550 to 650 is unchanged.

Orb, a usage-based billing platform, gives Adyen a route into AI-native companies, the company said. Since the deal closed, Adyen has won the payment volumes of several Orb clients, including Route and Wasabi Technologies.

Platforms Lead Growth Across Three Segments

Smaller merchants signed up through software platforms drove the fastest growth. Platforms net revenue rose 46% to €100.2 million, and 46 platform customers now process more than €1 billion a year, up from 37 a quarter earlier and 31 a year ago.

Q3 2026Net revenue (EUR)YoY changeConstant currencyProcessed volume growth
Digital387.4 million+16%+14%+28%
Unified Commerce250.5 million+29%+27%+22%
Platforms100.2 million+46%+44%+55%
Total738.1 million+23%+22%+30%

Unified Commerce, which combines in-store and online payments, grew 29% to €250.5 million with the first revenue from Talon.One, in what Adyen described as a subdued retail market. Digital, the largest segment, grew 16% to €387.4 million on higher volumes from its biggest customers.

Adyen's quarterly volume has grown about 41% in two years, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, from €320.6 billion in the third quarter of 2024.

Adyen kept its 2026 net revenue growth forecast of 21% to 23% at constant currency. It expects capital expenditure of 7% of net revenue this year, falling back toward historical levels after 2026.

Niclas Neglen, nominated as chief financial officer, is due to start on February 1, 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.

title: NYSE to Launch All-or-Nothing Options on Apple, Nvidia and Tesla Shares
summary:

content:
2026-10-28T10:46:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 08:46 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The contracts pay a fixed sum or nothing, depending on where a stock closes, and could trade within days.
  • Separate $1 contracts on company earnings figures still await SEC approval, after Cboe won clearance.

The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) plans to start trading all-or-nothing options on 12 stocks and exchange-traded funds within days, Reuters reported yesterday (Tuesday). The first underlyings include Apple, Nvidia, Tesla and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

The contracts, called binary return options, pay a fixed amount if a share closes above or below a set price, and nothing if it does not. NYSE plans to add more underlyings over time.

US demand for yes-or-no bets has grown fast. Monthly event contract volume rose from about $1 billion in 2024 to more than $50 billion in July 2026, the Committee on Capital Markets Regulation said this month in a letter backing Cboe's plan for contracts on company earnings figures.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Three US Exchanges, Three Stages

NYSE joins Cboe and MEMX in bringing binary contracts to US options markets this year, and each exchange sits at a different stage.

Cboe has listed yes-or-no options on the Mini-S&P 500 since June, starting with Interactive Brokers, and Charles Schwab plans to offer them to its clients.

Its earnings contracts are next. The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC ) cleared them on October 13 with Robinhood lined up as the first retail broker, and Cboe's clearing house won temporary SEC registration on October 23. Cboe plans to list them in the fourth quarter.

MEMX filed for similar earnings contracts in August and NYSE in September. That leaves Cboe's index options as the only one of these products already trading, with four more in the queue.

A Product First Approved in 2007

The single-stock contracts run under rules NYSE American has carried for years. The SEC approved them in August 2007 as Fixed Return Options on stocks and ETFs, when the venue was still the American Stock Exchange.

The exchange limited them to closing trades in March 2009 and won SEC approval in 2014 to relaunch them as Binary Return Derivatives, filings show. NYSE describes each contract as paying a fixed $100.

"We've seen this incredible growth in the US options market over the last several years," Kevin Tyrrell, NYSE's chief product officer, told Reuters.

The earnings contracts NYSE is still waiting on would pay $1 or nothing. The payout depends on whether a figure reported to the SEC, such as Apple's iPhone sales or Tesla's Model 3/Y production, meets a strike. The filings list 23 companies, from JPMorgan Chase to SpaceX.

Europe Keeps the Payout From Retail

The same all-or-nothing payout is closed to retail clients in Europe. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) barred binary option sales to retail investors in 2018 and said in July that event contracts classed as financial instruments fall under the same bans.

Britain followed. The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) made its own retail ban permanent in April 2019.

NYSE's owner is also invested in prediction markets. Intercontinental Exchange agreed in October 2025 to invest up to $2 billion in prediction market Polymarket and completed the commitment in March.

title: Plus500 Starts Offering Kalshi’s Never-Expiring Futures in the US
summary:
Plus500 started offering Kalshi's perpetual futures through its US brokerage today (Wednesday). It said it is the first futures commission merchant (FCM) to do so apart from Kalshi Prime, the exchange's own brokerage.
Perpetual futures, or perps, never expire, so traders can hold a position without ...
content:
2026-10-28T10:16:24.032+02:00

Wednesday, 28/10/2026 | 08:16 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The broker clears the contracts itself and went live before Webull, which plans to offer them from November.
  • Kalshi says its perps traded $5.5 billion in their first two weeks after the CFTC approved them in May.

Plus500 started offering Kalshi's perpetual futures through its US brokerage today (Wednesday). It said it is the first futures commission merchant (FCM) to do so apart from Kalshi Prime, the exchange's own brokerage.

Perpetual futures, or perps, never expire, so traders can hold a position without rolling it into a new contract. Plus500 executes, routes and clears the trades on its own systems, as a clearing member of Kalshi Klear.

The contracts are new to regulated US markets and have drawn volume quickly. Kalshi said its perps traded more than $5.5 billion in their first two weeks after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC ) approved the first one in May.

Plus500 is offering them to institutional clients and to partner brokers that run their customers' trading on its systems.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Webull Plans the Same Contracts From November

Outside brokers are only starting to carry Kalshi's perps, and the announcements so far put Plus500 first to go live. Webull said on October 20 that eligible US customers will get Kalshi-listed crypto perps through Webull Futures accounts from November, also cleared by Kalshi Klear.

Plus500 Chief Executive David Zruia said the product's "arrival on a fully regulated US exchange is a significant boost for the whole industry."

Crypto exchanges reached US traders by other means. Coinbase runs perpetual-style futures that settle funding twice a day, and Kraken has a US venue with 16 contracts, FinanceMagnates.com reported in June.

Volume on the exchange has kept building since launch. Kalshi's crypto perps had generated about $16.1 billion in volume by late July, roughly three times the two-week figure, before the exchange added commodities and indices.

Event Contracts Came First

Perps are the latest step in Plus500's US push. It began clearing event contracts in December for the prediction markets platform backed by CME Group and FanDuel.

Two months later it added Kalshi's prediction markets to its US futures business, clearing those trades directly as well.

Kalshi Chief Executive Tarek Mansour said Plus500 "was the natural choice to support our expansion into perpetual futures."

Non-OTC products, which include its US futures business, still made up about 16% of revenue in the first nine months, Plus500 said in its third-quarter update on Monday.

The rest still comes from contracts for difference, a business whose quarterly volumes FM Intelligence tracks across 186 retail brokers.

Plus500 is also building a US super-app for the first quarter of 2027 and buying a US broker, Hedge Capital Markets, pending approval from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

CME Is Challenging the Approval

The product still faces a legal fight. CME is suing the CFTC in federal court over the May approval of Kalshi's bitcoin perpetual, arguing the contract is a swap and should be regulated as one.

Kalshi has meanwhile kept adding contracts. It opened a perpetual on a US large-cap stock index on October 6, and its market page showed $556,000 in 24-hour volume and $219,600 in open interest that evening.

title: Best Crypto to Buy Now: MemeToro ($MT) AI Presale at $0.00649 vs Pepe, Solana and Dogecoin
summary: Best crypto to buy now? MemeToro ($MT), an open-source AI presale on BNB Chain at $0.00649, leads this list ahead of Solana, Dogecoin, Pepe and Bitcoin, with the Fed meeting and BTC price in view.
content:
Skip to content

Best crypto to buy now? MemeToro ($MT), an open-source AI presale on BNB Chain at $0.00649, leads this list ahead of Solana, Dogecoin, Pepe and Bitcoin, with the Fed meeting and BTC price in view.

Key takeaways

  • MemeToro ($MT) leads this list of the best crypto to buy now.
  • MemeToro is an open-source AI memecoin launchpad on BNB Chain; its presale is at Stage 9, $0.00649 per $MT. $500 buys about 77,042 $MT before fees.
  • Bitcoin trades near $80,000 and the Fed decision is due Wednesday, October 28; rate news moves altcoins and presale sentiment.
  • The $MT token contract is audited by Coinsult, BlockSAFU and SolidProof.

The best crypto to buy now depends on what you want from the market: a listed asset such as Bitcoin, Solana or Dogecoin, or an early-stage AI presale you can still inspect. MemeToro($MT) is the second kind and leads this list: an open-source AI memecoin launchpad on BNB Chain, now at Stage 9 of its crypto presale at $0.00649 per token, with $174K raised.

The best crypto to buy now: quick list

# Asset Type What to know Status
1 MemeToro ($MT) AI memecoin launchpad token, BNB Chain Open code, audited token, BSC Testnet launchpad contracts Presale, Stage 9
2 Solana (SOL) Layer-1 blockchain Fast chain; home of many memecoins Listed
3 Dogecoin (DOGE) Original memecoin, own chain Launched 2013; no fixed supply cap [verify] Listed
4 Pepe (PEPE) Meme token on Ethereum Launched 2023; value driven by attention Listed
5 Bitcoin (BTC) Store-of-value benchmark 21 million cap; sets market mood Listed

Bitcoin price today and the Fed meeting: what the market is watching

Bitcoin is trading near $80,000 and Ethereum near $2,300 as of October 27, 2026 [refresh on publish day]. The next move in both depends heavily on the Federal Reserve: the FOMC decision is due Wednesday, October 28 at 2:00 p.m. Eastern, with a press conference at 2:30 p.m., according to TronWeekly. Markets expect the Fed to hold rates; that report cites the target range at 3.75%-4.00% and about a 9% chance of a 25 basis point hike on CME FedWatch, while KuCoin’s market note cites a 72% probability of a pause [sources differ; check CME FedWatch].

  • Why it matters: a hawkish signal, for example hints of a December hike, tends to pressure risk assets, and altcoins and presales are usually the most sensitive.
  • A hold with neutral language usually removes one uncertainty, but it does not make any single coin safer.
  • Watch the press conference tone, not only the rate.

For presale buyers the lesson is practical: stage prices are fixed by the project, but the market a token lists into is not. Size any position as if the Fed week could go either way. This is context, not a forecast.ñ

1. MemeToro ($MT): the AI crypto presale at the top of this list

MemeToro is an open-source AI meme launch agent. It finds timely ideas from news, trends, culture and markets, then publishes a memecoin proposal with its reasoning, so readers can see why a coin should exist before deciding. The stated design principle is that the agent proposes and public smart contracts, not the AI or a private backend, enforce the funding and launch rules.

How the AI agent pipeline works

  • Signals: a dependency-free connector pulls worldwide-news and X trend signals, and keeps the evidence links with each signal.
  • Validation: the pipeline turns signals into one validated draft manifest, and rejects unverified evidence and insider token allocations.
  • Transparency: it publishes the shortlist of rejected candidates, and is built to decline to launch when nothing is suitable.
  • Run window: agent/run-window.mjs produces one window and publishes it to a test network.
  • Output: each proposal carries the concept, evidence, reasoning, token and funding parameters, and a machine-readable manifest.

How the contracts are designed

  • FairLaunchEscrow.sol: a funding escrow that holds one launch round and sets the round’s terms at creation (cap, deadline, threshold, allocation).
  • Launch manifest digest: each manifest commits to a digest of itself and its image, so anyone can check that the on-chain round matches the published terms. The README does not name the digest algorithm.
  • Factory: lists rounds for an ERC-8004 agent [verify the agent registration].
  • Executor interface: intended for token creation and liquidity provision; not yet implemented.
  • Rules by design: fixed-rate rounds (planned to accept BNB, selected stablecoins and $MT), wallet limits, no owner, admin role or upgrade path, and no founder or private allocation; any rounding remainder goes to liquidity. Per the project’s description of the design.
  • Test suite: the contract suite deploys a round from the published manifest and checks that the enforced terms match the published terms. ABIs and deploy scripts are published.

The repository is public under an MIT license and targets BNB Smart Chain, and the project reports 1,373 lines of Solidity in a recent development release.

What is built and what is not

Component Status per the README
Agent data connector and manifest pipeline Implemented, tested
Escrow and factory drafts with tests, ABIs Implemented as drafts
Test-network window script Implemented
Hourly autonomous service Not implemented
Token creation and liquidity (executor) Not implemented
Independent security review of launch contracts Planned; launch contracts are unaudited and not deployed

The $MT token contract has been audited by Coinsult, SolidProof and BlockSAFU. That covers the $MT token. The launchpad contracts are a separate, unfinished body of work: the README advises against using the repository to hold real funds. A public roadmap covers hosting published manifests, a listing page, hourly runs, token creation and liquidity, ERC-8004 reputation and independent security reviews.

title: Ripple Expands BNY Deal to Bring $2.5B RLUSD and XRP Into Trade Finance
summary:
Key Takeaways: BNY extended the existing partnership relationship with Ripple by adding XRP as its digital asset to its digital asset custody platform, along with the RLUSD stablecoin. The parties
The post Ripple Expands BNY Deal to Bring $2.5B RLUSD and XRP Into Trade Finance appeared first on Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • BNY extended the existing partnership relationship with Ripple by adding XRP as its digital asset to its digital asset custody platform, along with the RLUSD stablecoin.
  • The parties will consider onboarding tokenized assets to the XRP Ledger (XRPL) and direct RLUSD minting and redemption transactions with BNY.
  • Ripple, BNY and C2FO are looking into supply chain finance to expand investor access to tokenized trade finance.

Ripple is building out its institutional crypto infrastructure in a more multi-platform levelled partnership with BNY, which is increasingly digitising asset custody services and introducing trade finance functions. Announced on October 27, 2026, the agreement builds on their existing relationship and targets practical uses for blockchain technology across financial markets.

Trade finance is coming to the XRP Ledger!

Today, we’re expanding our collaboration with @BNYglobal across custody and tokenized trade finance, bringing BNY’s institutional scale together with $RLUSD, @XRP and the XRP Ledger.

→ https://t.co/0wOltZclRj https://t.co/3LRULGEuqO

— Ripple (@Ripple) October 27, 2026

  • BNY Expands XRP and RLUSD Custody Services
  • Ripple Targets Tokenized Trade Finance on XRPL
    • How Tokenized Receivables Could Work

BNY Expands XRP and RLUSD Custody Services

BNY has also announced the addition of XRP, the native token on the XRP Ledger, and Ripple’s USD-pegged RLUSD, a stablecoin to its Digital Asset Custody platform. The move builds upon a collaboration where BNY is currently the primary reserve custodian for RLUSD and has custody of Ripple Prime.

The new service aims to protect, collect and move digital assets by eligible institutional investors in BNY’s existing custody framework. This offers another way for financial institutions to manage XRP and RLUSD without having to use just crypto-native custody providers.

Additionally, BNY will collaborate with Ripple to give its clients the ability to mint and redeem RLUSD directly at the bank. The target functionality will make access to the stablecoin easier for those that qualify, but it hasn’t been revealed when this will be available.

Ripple’s president, Monica Long, said that they are moving past just issuing digital assets on blockchain networks to making them usable for financial markets, as payment and as collateral.

Read More: Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight

Ripple Targets Tokenized Trade Finance on XRPL

The partnership is also broader than just tokens to include investment products that may be introduced on the XRP Ledger. Ripple and BNY will look to mature these opportunities as use cases and institutional demand on the network grows.

They have also been looking at a project in the trade finance area, in collaboration with a global working-capital platform called C2FO. The aim of the effort is to reach a more invested audience for trade finance assets, such as approved receivables.

How Tokenized Receivables Could Work

A business could experience trade receivables when a customer orders and pays for a product before they receive it. These financial claims can be tokenized to give them a digital counterpart that can be managed and potentially given through a blockchain-based infrastructure.

Aligned loans and financing for approved receivables may be helpful for suppliers’ working-capital requirements during the payment delay. Depends on the structure of the assets and applicable requirements, but investors could also be able to receive a wider selection of financing options.

The Ripple-BNY-C2FO project is however at an exploratory stage. The announcement does not guarantee a live product, closed transactions or particular decreases in financing and settlement time.

title: NBA Taps Kalshi and Polymarket in Prediction Markets Deal With CFTC Safeguards
summary:
Key Takeaways: The NBA has decided Kalshi and Polymarket to be its preferred prediction market exchanges. The two platforms will be equipped with official NBA data via Sportradar. The league
The post NBA Taps Kalshi and Polymarket in Prediction Markets Deal With CFTC Safeguards appeared first on Cry...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The NBA has decided Kalshi and Polymarket to be its preferred prediction market exchanges.
  • The two platforms will be equipped with official NBA data via Sportradar.
  • The league also inked a CFTC agreement that addressed issues of insider trading and market integrity.

The NBA is moving deeper into prediction markets through new commercial deals with Kalshi and Polymarket, while adding tighter safeguards around sports-related event contracts.

The league also inked a Memorandum of Understanding with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, establishing a new agreement on how information and integrity monitoring is shared.

  • NBA Names Kalshi and Polymarket Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges
  • Official NBA Data Will Help Settle Event Contracts
    • CFTC Deal Targets Insider Trading and Fraud
    • Prediction Markets Gain Deeper Sports Integration

NBA Names Kalshi and Polymarket Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges

The new deals make Kalshi and Polymarket the NBA’s top pick’s sportsbook exchanges.

Both systems will be granted NBA IP, marketing and promotional rights within the United States, as well as have access to official NBA data provided by Sportradar for approved NBA markets.

Agreements also include measures to combat market abuse. Trading of NBA event contracts is prohibited between NBA and NBA team personnel and the NBA and the NBA team must cooperate in investigations and suspicious trades.

The NBA told us that ensuring integrity of the game is always our No. 1 focus, as prediction markets grow in fan involvement.

Read More: Polymarket Fires CMO After Fake-Trade Probe

Official NBA Data Will Help Settle Event Contracts

Access to official Sportradar data is a key part of the partnerships. Prediction markets rely on accurate event results on which to set their contracts. The agreement between Kalshi and Polymarket and the official NBA data feed reduces the chance of disputes about the results of basketball games, and provides a more uniform framework for accepted markets.

The league also extended an agreement with DraftKings to include prediction markets and promotion across the country. Additional operators will be added in the next few weeks.

CFTC Deal Targets Insider Trading and Fraud

The NBA’s different MOU with the CFTC centres on the exchange of information and the assurance of fair and transparent prediction markets.

The agreement will foster closer partnerships to combat abuses including insider trading and fraud, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said. With the NBA now following suit, the Major League Baseball and NHL have each signed similar agreements with the regulator.

The significance of the arrangement lies in the fact that the NBA will have private information that could impact the pricing of event contracts, such as players’ availability, injuries, internal NBA development or other private information.

Prediction Markets Gain Deeper Sports Integration

These deals illustrate how prediction websites are increasingly gaining official sporting ground as opposed to just being a place to trade. Kalshi has already launched federally regulated event contracts in the U.S. and Polymarket has amassed a substantial audience on the crypto side of the prediction market.

The NBA’s actions put basketball contracts in a useful commercial and data environment. Also, the league is tightening up around who is allowed to trade and what suspicious activity is done.

Continued activity related to NBA event contracts is also evident in CFTC filings, such as certified binary products linked to specific games, as well as other basketball-related events.

title: Ripple Partners With Robinhood to Bring $2.4B RLUSD to 28.6M Customers
summary:
Key Takeaways: RLUSD, treasury management and institutional trading come together in Ripple and Robinhood partnership. RLUSD appears on the Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp exchange, and its app is scheduled for
The post Ripple Partners With Robinhood to Bring $2.4B RLUSD to 28.6M Customers appeared fir...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • RLUSD, treasury management and institutional trading come together in Ripple and Robinhood partnership.
  • RLUSD appears on the Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp exchange, and its app is scheduled for launch later this year.
  • Robinhood will incorporate Ripple Treasury and Ripple Prime will build on its financing and trading offerings.

Ripple is deepening its ties with Robinhood in a deal that connects stablecoin adoption with institutional crypto infrastructure. Announced on October 27, 2026, the partnership spans retail access, institutional settlement, corporate treasury operations, and digital asset financing.

  • RLUSD Expands Across Robinhood’s Crypto Ecosystem
  • Robinhood Adds Ripple Treasury and Institutional Financing
    • Ripple Prime Expands Trading and Financing Access
    • Stablecoins Move Beyond Crypto Trading

RLUSD Expands Across Robinhood’s Crypto Ecosystem

Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, RLUSD, will play a central role in the expanded partnership. The token already exists in Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp by Robinhood, and it should be out in the Robinhood app later this year.

Ripple also intends to integrate RLUSD on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) for institutional settlement, taking the stablecoin beyond retail crypto transactions.

According to Ripple, RLUSD has raised its market cap to over $2.4 billion since it was launched in December 2024. Robinhood, meanwhile, has 28.6 million funded customers worldwide and provides access to a large retail and institutional financial network in that area.

Both companies have not revealed a retail launch date, any volume of transactions and financial value of the deal.

Read More: Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real Estate Deals

Robinhood Adds Ripple Treasury and Institutional Financing

It’s not just about the distribution of the stablecoins. Through the integration of Ripple Treasury, Robinhood will automate various Robinhood financial functions, like cash management, liquidity, payment, cash-flow forecasting and risk management.

The integration will aim to make Robinhood’s own finance administration across business units and markets simpler.

Ripple Prime Expands Trading and Financing Access

Bitstamp by Robinhood will also improve their already existing partnership with Ripple Prime. Lending and margin financing for about 20 digital assets are currently available, and there is a Bitstamp spot trading service for Ripple Prime clients.

The announcement indicates that Bitstamp plans to roll out perpetual futures trading later in 2026. These services empower stablecoins to be matched with settlement and financing services, ultimately establishing a wider linkage between the two firms beyond a mere listing of tokens.

Read More: Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight

Stablecoins Move Beyond Crypto Trading

The deal comes at a time when the stablecoin market continues to grow. Stablecoin supplies have climbed above $300 billion, with the growing influence of tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar, according to Ripple.

Stablecoins can help with the settlement and payment aspects of the blockchain and lower the risk of price fluctuations of assets like XRP and Bitcoin. However, the usefulness in institutional markets is determined by liquidity, regulation and suitability to integrate with the existing financial systems.

The co-operation doesn’t mandate that RB has to buy XRP or that it be a bridge asset in every transaction conducted within RLUSD. The announcement, however, particularizes RLUSD for institutional placement on XRPL, as well as separate integrations of treasury and financing.

title: Bitget Wallet Officially Launches Virtual Accounts to 100M Crypto Users
summary:
Key Takeaways: Bitget Wallet introduces free USD & EUR virtual accounts. All deposits automatically go to USDT or USDC. The fee for making a $500 ACH transfer is approximately $2.
The post Bitget Wallet Officially Launches Virtual Accounts to 100M Crypto Users appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Bitget Wallet introduces free USD & EUR virtual accounts.
  • All deposits automatically go to USDT or USDC.
  • The fee for making a $500 ACH transfer is approximately $2.

Bitget Wallet is evolving from a crypto storage and trading platform to a service that allows users to receive traditional currencies. Launched on October 27, 2026, Virtual Accounts gives users personal USD and EUR account details directly inside the wallet, without requiring local residency or a branch visit.

What if you could have your own US or EU bank account, with just a few taps?

INTRODUCING: Virtual Accounts – dedicated USD & EUR accounts inside Bitget Wallet.

Get paid. Receive money. Fund your wallet. No walls. No borders. No banks.

Just your money in your wallet. https://t.co/94453fCgl9

— Bitget Wallet 🩵 (@BitgetWallet) October 27, 2026

  • Bitget Wallet Connects Bank Transfers to Stablecoins
  • $500 Transfers Could Cost Just $2 in Platform Fees
    • Who Can Benefit From Virtual Accounts?

Bitget Wallet Connects Bank Transfers to Stablecoins

The new Virtual Accounts service is available via a licensed financial infrastructure partner, Noah. Users can set up USD and EUR accounts for free and have access to payments via recognized banking networks.

These e-payment options all detail ACH, Fedwire (U.S.), SEPA (Europe), or SWIFT (international). The user deposits money and the money is instantly converted into USDT/USDC and deposited into the user’s self-custodial wallet.

This setup allows the users to flow the payment straight into crypto directly without having to go over a centralized exchange or a separate crypto on-ramp.

The stablecoins can then be utilized throughout the services existing in Bitget Wallet, including card spending, QR payments, cross-border transfers, yield products, and investments in cryptocurrencies and tokenized real-world assets.

The service is available to accept incoming transfers, at this time, however. The decision indicates that outbound bank transfers will be scheduled for the coming months, the announcement said.

Read More: Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange

$500 Transfers Could Cost Just $2 in Platform Fees

One of the major selling points is the fact that it could cut out on any bills related to cross border payments, especially for freelancers, beneficiaries of overseas income or people that work remotely.

The estimated platform fee for transferring $500 ACH via Virtual Accounts is about $2 on Bitget Wallet. In comparison, World Bank data shows that the average remittance cost around the world is about 6%, or roughly $30 on the same transmission.

The comparison implies that there is a significant potential saving, but the numbers are not necessarily comparable in all cases. Few charges may not be included for sending-bank charges, blockchain network charges, and third-party charges.

Who Can Benefit From Virtual Accounts?

The feature targets three main groups, which are crypto users intending to deposit with a traditional bank and convert to stablecoins, those receiving international remittances, and workers receiving salaries from abroad with either a US or European employer.

A personal USD and EUR account may present another easy method for receiving foreign-currency payments for eligible users who do not have foreign-currency bank accounts. The money is then moved to what is called “under wallet custody”, where it is still held in the user’s wallet and not deposited in a traditional bank account.

According to Bitget Wallet, they have over 100 million users globally and have more than $300 million in user protection funds. In addition to the already existing crypto-linked cards and QR payments capabilities, Virtual Accounts also introduces the receiving feature into its wider payment platform.

The contracts provide exposure to company-linked price movements without ownership of the underlying shares.

title: Chainlink Targets $700B Custody Market With CustodySync and Anchorage DeFi Access
summary:
Key Takeaways: Chainlink introduced CustodySync, a new solution that connects loan markets in DeFi and qualified custody. The launch partner is Anchorage Digital Bank, with institutional clients able to borrow
The post Chainlink Targets $700B Custody Market With CustodySync and Anchorage DeFi Access...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Chainlink introduced CustodySync, a new solution that connects loan markets in DeFi and qualified custody.
  • The launch partner is Anchorage Digital Bank, with institutional clients able to borrow collateral that stays in Anchorage.
  • According to Chainlink, there are approximately $700 billion of digital assets caged in custodians and could be directed toward onchain lending.

Chainlink is enabling an alternative path for institutional funds to join the DeFi space without moving assets out of regulated custody.

The company introduced CustodySync with Anchorage Digital Bank as its first partner, targeting institutions that want DeFi liquidity but still need qualified custody, internal controls and strict risk management.

  • Chainlink CustodySync Connects $700B in Custodied Crypto to DeFi
  • Collateral Stays in Custody While Loans Move Onchain
    • Chainlink Uses CRE, Proof of Reserve and Data Feeds in One Stack

Chainlink CustodySync Connects $700B in Custodied Crypto to DeFi

Traditional custody markets account for about $250 trillion, according to Chainlink, compared to an estimated $700 billion worth of digital assets in custody. Meanwhile, DeFi lending markets have over $30 billion in active locked-up loans and over $80 billion in deposits.

Its purpose is to harmonize those two systems, CustodySync. An institution does not have to move the assets to the lending protocol, it can hold them with a qualified custodian and then put them to use onchain to borrow.

Anchorage Digital Bank serves as the official launch partner and uses its Atlas Collateral Management infrastructure to coordinate collateral, margin monitoring and liquidation processes.

Read More: SEC Proposes New Crypto Custody Rules to Unlock Multi-Trillion Dollar Market Access

Collateral Stays in Custody While Loans Move Onchain

The balance of collateral remains in the control of the custodian with the structure. Chainlink Proof of Reserve publishes the custody balances onchain, and a transfer restricted receipt token is the collateral in the lending market. The token mirrors the amount held in custody but does not create an independent claim outside the lending arrangement.

The borrowed assets then flow directly from the DeFi market to the institutional borrower.

Chainlink Data Feeds would feed prices to the lending protocol, while Data Streams would pass the prices up to the custodian’s off-chain systems. That helps to minimize the potential for the two parties to do inconsistent liquidations or for them to determine different loan-to-value ratios.

Chainlink Uses CRE, Proof of Reserve and Data Feeds in One Stack

CustodySync combines several Chainlink products into a single institutional workflow.

The Chainlink Runtime Environment is responsible for managing interactions between the custody systems and the onchain markets. Proof of Reserve is used to complete balance checks on the system and Data Feeds and Data Streams help to ensure the values of the collaterals are consistent across both environments.

When a position exceeds its limits, the appointed collateral agent ensures the process of a sale is run. During liquidation, CustodySync makes sure the lending position doesn’t lose synchronization by onboarding the proceeds onchain before final settlement.

Anchorage Digital Bank is the first qualified custodian to have implemented CustodySync. They said the bank’s already had collateral management working on its Atlas instruments for institutional loans, monitoring, as well as margin call and margin liquidation workflows.

title: Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ripple received final OCC authorization for its national trust bank. The bank will back up both reserves (RLUSD) and digital asset custody. RLUSD’s market value has increased to
The post Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple received final OCC authorization for its national trust bank.
  • The bank will back up both reserves (RLUSD) and digital asset custody.
  • RLUSD’s market value has increased to approximately $2.5 billion.

Ripple has cleared a major U.S. regulatory hurdle, securing final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Under the latest move, Ripple will have a federally-supervised company to operate portions of the stablecoin and custody services, while issuance of its stable coin remains in Ripple’s existing New York state-licensed trust company.

  • Ripple National Trust Bank Gets Final Federal Approval
  • RLUSD Keeps State Oversight While Adding a Federal Layer
    • $2.5B RLUSD Gets a Bigger Institutional Role
    • OCC Charter Expands Ripple’s Crypto Banking Footprint

Ripple National Trust Bank Gets Final Federal Approval

According to Ripple, the OCC granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), after receiving preliminary conditional approval in December 2025.

The bank’s authorized activities include servicing segregated reserves of Ripple USD, as a collateral trustee, and as a fiduciary asset custodian for digital assets.

The original OCC approval already included provisions for a national trust bank to provide collateral trustee services and for cryptocurrency custodial services. The same limited-purpose trust company, Standard Custody & Trust Company (SCTC) pursuant to license by the New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), will continue to be the issuer of RLUSD.

Read More: Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real Estate Deals

RLUSD Keeps State Oversight While Adding a Federal Layer

That setup provides Ripple with two layers of regulation on its stablecoin system. Custody remains with Standard, but OCC supervision of custody and reserve functions added by Ripple National Trust Bank. Ripple reports that the BNY remains RLUSD’s primary reserve custodian.

The stablecoin is collateralized by a combination of U.S. dollar deposits and government securities and other cash-equivalent assets, with reserves and circulating supply attested to third-party monthly.

$2.5B RLUSD Gets a Bigger Institutional Role

Since its launch in December 2024, Ripple has made it to a market cap of $2.5 billion, said RLUSD.

The stablecoin has already hit the Ripple payments system, and is collateralized in Ripple Prime. With the new trust bank, Ripple now has a regulated path for it to explore some of its institutional applications like settlement, custody, and treasury.

Ripple’s CEO, Brad Garlinghouse, said the approval was evidence that crypto can thrive in the traditional financial system instead of on its own outside it. Over the past few years, the firm has made a recurring theme of its play with the introduction of regulated infrastructure, from payments and stablecoins to custody and capital markets.

Big news heading into @RippleSwell: the @USOCC has granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.

This gives Ripple a federally supervised platform to support $RLUSD and provide digital asset custody to enterprises.

We’ve always said crypto and banks work better together — this is what that looks like. Real innovation, real accountability, federal oversight.

The revolution isn’t happening outside the system. It’s happening from within it.

— Brad Garlinghouse (@bgarlinghouse) October 26, 2026

Read More: Ripple and Arf Bring $10B PayFi Settlement Liquidity to XRP Ledger With RLUSD

OCC Charter Expands Ripple’s Crypto Banking Footprint

The national trust bank is a narrow bank as compared to a commercial bank. It tends to concentrate on the custody, fiduciary and asset management operations, as opposed to traditional deposit and lending activities.

The OCC has increased its pandemic-era flexibility on digital-asset companies establishing federal charters. In December 2025, Ripple was conditionally approved along with a number of other applicants for crypto-focused trust banks.

The broader regulatory framework is also changing. In October 2026, the OCC finalized rules that implement portions of the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoins, which take effect in January 2027.

As a result of getting the thumbs up, Ripple can now shift its focus from Charter preparation to running a federally supervised digital-centric bank that will be trust banks for institutional custody and stablecoins.
